configure-redis-using-configmap.md.summary: This page demonstrates how to configure Redis using a ConfigMap, showing the process of creating a ConfigMap with Redis configuration values, mounting a Redis Pod to use it, and verifying the configuration via Redis CLI.

configure-runasusername.md.title: Configure RunAsUserName for Windows pods and containers
configure-runasusername.md.summary: This guide explains how to set the `runAsUserName` setting for Windows pods and containers using Kubernetes manifests, allowing pods to run as a specific user on Windows nodes.

configure-service-account.md.title: Configure Service Accounts for Pods
configure-service-account.md.summary: This guide explains how to configure ServiceAccounts for Pods in Kubernetes, detailing how Pods authenticate as ServiceAccounts, how to opt out of API credential automounting, and the automatic revocation of credentials when Pods are deleted.

configure-upgrade-etcd.md.title: Operating etcd clusters for Kubernetes
configure-upgrade-etcd.md.summary: This guide explains how to deploy, manage, and restore etcd clusters for Kubernetes, emphasizing leader-based architecture, odd-numbered member requirements, and resource isolation for stable production deployments.

configure-volume-storage.md.title: Configure a Pod to Use a Volume for Storage
configure-volume-storage.md.summary: This page explains how to configure a Kubernetes Pod to use a Volume for persistent storage, specifically using an emptyDir volume that persists the container's filesystem state even after the container terminates and restarts.

connect-applications-service.md.title: Connecting Applications with Services
connect-applications-service.md.summary: This guide explains the Kubernetes networking model where pods communicate directly without explicit host-to-pod mappings, allowing services to be exposed across the cluster. It details how to create a Service to abstract pods and define their unique IPs, ensuring reliable service discovery even after pod failures.

connecting-frontend-backend.md.title: Connect a Frontend to a Backend Using Services
connecting-frontend-backend.md.summary: This guide demonstrates how to create a frontend microservice and a backend microservice using Kubernetes, deploying a hello greeter backend and exposing it via a LoadBalancer service.

container-env-variables.md.title: Container Environment Variables
container-env-variables.md.summary: Container environment variables are name=value pairs defining useful information for running containers within pods, including file system details and cluster resources.

container-environment.md.title: Container Environment
container-environment.md.summary: This page describes the Kubernetes container environment, detailing filesystems (images and volumes), container information (hostname, pod name), and cluster services (services with dedicated IPs and DNS support).

container-lifecycle-hooks.md.title: Container Lifecycle Hooks
container-lifecycle-hooks.md.summary: This page explains how Kubernetes manages Containers using the hook framework to run code triggered by events during their lifecycle, including PostStart, PreStop, and StopSignal hooks.

container-runtime.md.title: Container Runtime
container-runtime.md.summary: This page explains Kubernetes' container runtime, detailing how it manages container execution and lifecycle within the Kubernetes environment, including supported runtimes like containerd and cri-o.

container-runtimes.md.title: Container Runtimes
container-runtimes.md.summary: This page outlines how to install and configure container runtimes (like containerd, CRI-O, Docker, and Mirantis) on Linux nodes within a Kubernetes cluster, emphasizing the need for a CRI-compliant runtime and managing cgroup drivers for resource management.

container.md.title: Container
container.md.summary: This page explains containers as lightweight, portable executable images that decouple applications from host infrastructure, enabling easier deployment and scaling across cloud or OS environments.

containerd.md.title: containerd
containerd.md.summary: A lightweight container runtime built for simplicity and portability, handling image fetching, execution, and networking.

containers.md.title: Containers
containers.md.summary: This page explains containers, container images, and their use in operations. It details how containers decouple applications from host infrastructure, are stateless and immutable, and how RuntimeClass allows different pods to run with different container runtime settings.

contributor.md.title: Contributor
contributor.md.summary: A role where individuals donate code, documentation, or time to help the Kubernetes project or community, including PRs, issues, SIG participation, and organizing events.

control-plane-flags.md.title: Customizing components with the kubeadm API
control-plane-flags.md.summary: This page explains how to customize control plane components like APIServer, ControllerManager, and Scheduler using the kubeadm API, including flags in ClusterConfiguration and patches per-node.

control-plane-node-communication.md.title: Communication between Nodes and the Control Plane
control-plane-node-communication.md.summary: This document details the secure communication paths between the Kubernetes API server and nodes, including the hub-and-spoke architecture where API requests terminate at the kubelet. It specifies that the API server uses HTTPS (port 443) with client certificates for authentication, and pods can connect securely via service accounts. The control plane communicates with nodes over the same secure port, enabling untrusted network deployments.

control-plane.md.title: Control Plane
control-plane.md.summary: This page describes the container orchestration layer that exposes APIs for defining, deploying, and managing container lifecycles, composed of components like etcd, API Server, and Scheduler.

controller-manager-leader-migration.md.title: Migrate Replicated Control Plane To Use Cloud Controller Manager
controller-manager-leader-migration.md.summary: This guide details the process of migrating replicated control plane components from the kube-controller-manager to the cloud-controller-manager, enabling leader migration for HA clusters.

controller.md.title: Controllers
controller.md.summary: This page explains the Controllers pattern in robotics and automation, detailing how controllers track Kubernetes resources, manage state via API server interactions, and handle direct control of external systems.

controllers.md.title: Kubernetes Workload Management
controllers.md.summary: Kubernetes provides declarative APIs for managing workloads, including Deployments for stateless apps, StatefulSets for persistent pods with identity, and DaemonSets for node-specific drivers. It automates Pod replacement and manages cluster networking, essential for container orchestration.

controlling-access.md.title: Controlling Access to the Kubernetes API
controlling-access.md.summary: This page explains how to control access to the Kubernetes API, detailing TLS security, authentication steps, and authorization processes for both human users and service accounts.

coordinated-leader-election.md.title: Coordinated Leader Election
coordinated-leader-election.md.summary: Kubernetes enables leader selection via coordinated leader election to satisfy version skew constraints. This feature allows control plane components (kube-controller-manager and kube-scheduler) to automatically elect a leader using the Lease API, which acts as a distributed lock to prevent race conditions during cluster upgrades.

coredns.md.title: Using CoreDNS for Service Discovery
coredns.md.summary: This page outlines the upgrade process and installation steps for CoreDNS, including manual deployment instructions and the kubeadm tool for automatic retention. It also details tuning options and provides links to documentation on scaling and the Kubernetes plugin.

cpu-constraint-namespace.md.title: Configure Minimum and Maximum CPU Constraints for a Namespace
cpu-constraint-namespace.md.summary: This page explains how to set Kubernetes limits on CPU resources for containers and Pods within a namespace, ensuring pods meet minimum and maximum CPU requirements.

cpu-default-namespace.md.title: Configure Default CPU Requests and Limits for a Namespace
cpu-default-namespace.md.summary: This page explains how to set default CPU requests and limits for a Kubernetes namespace, including how pods without explicit limits default to 0.5 request and 1 limit, and how to override these defaults with custom manifests.

cpu-management-policies.md.title: Control CPU Management Policies on the Node
cpu-management-policies.md.summary: This page explains how Kubernetes manages CPU policies for pods on nodes, detailing default CFS-based scheduling, alternative policies for high-latency workloads, and Windows-specific CPU Manager features.

create-cluster-kubeadm.md.title: Creating a cluster with kubeadm
create-cluster-kubeadm.md.summary: This guide explains how to create a Kubernetes cluster using the kubeadm tool, covering prerequisites like Linux OS and RAM, objectives of installing a control-plane node and a pod network, and installation steps for both new and existing hosts.

create-daemon-set.md.title: Building a Basic DaemonSet
create-daemon-set.md.summary: This page demonstrates how to create a Kubernetes DaemonSet that runs a Pod on every node, using an init container to log host paths and a pause container to keep the Pod running.

create-external-load-balancer.md.title: Create an External Load Balancer
create-external-load-balancer.md.summary: This page explains how to create an external load balancer using YAML manifests or kubectl, including configuration for LoadBalancer type, ingress configuration, and how to find the load balancer's IP address.

create-hostprocess-pod.md.title: Windows HostProcess Containers
create-hostprocess-pod.md.summary: This guide explains how Windows HostProcess containers enable networked workloads on Windows nodes without requiring dedicated proxies, allowing administrators to deploy plugins and services while reducing privilege requirements.

cri-o.md.title: CRI-O
cri-o.md.summary: CRI-O is a Kubernetes tool that enables running OCI-compliant container runtimes via Kubernetes, allowing pods to use compatible runtimes and fetch OCI images from remote registries.

cri.md.title: Container Runtime Interface (CRI) API Reference
cri.md.summary: This page explains the CRI plugin interface used by kubelet to connect to various container runtimes, including v1 API support requirements, upgrade handling, and streaming RPCs for large-scale container lists.

crictl.md.title: Debugging Kubernetes nodes with crictl
crictl.md.summary: This page explains how to use crictl, a command-line interface for CRI-compatible container runtimes, to inspect and debug container runtimes and applications on a Kubernetes node.

cron-jobs.md.title: CronJob
cron-jobs.md.summary: CronJob is a scheduled job system that runs periodic tasks like backups and reports, functioning similarly to a crontab line on Unix systems.

csi.md.title: Container Storage Interface (CSI) - Kubernetes Storage Plugin
csi.md.summary: CSI defines a standard interface for Kubernetes to expose storage systems, enabling out-of-tree custom plugins that vendors can create without adding them to the repository.

custom-resource-definition-versioning.md.title: Versions in CustomResourceDefinitions
custom-resource-definition-versioning.md.summary: This page explains how to add versioning information to CustomResourceDefinitions to indicate stability levels and how to upgrade objects between API versions.

custom-resource-definitions.md.title: Extend the Kubernetes API with CustomResourceDefinitions
custom-resource-definitions.md.summary: This guide explains how to create a CustomResourceDefinition (CRD) in Kubernetes to extend the API with custom objects, including naming conventions, namespace management, and creating RESTful endpoints.

custom-resources.md.title: Custom Resources
custom-resources.md.summary: This page explains how to add custom resources to Kubernetes via API extensions, comparing declarative APIs with standalone services, and detailing how to choose between aggregating with the cluster or using a standalone API.

customize-hosts-file-for-pods.md.title: Adding entries to Pod /etc/hosts with HostAliases
customize-hosts-file-for-pods.md.summary: This guide explains how to add custom DNS entries to a Kubernetes Pod's /etc/hosts file using HostAliases in PodSpec, contrasting this with the recommended kubelet-managed approach.

customresourcedefinition.md.title: CustomResourceDefinition
customresourcedefinition.md.summary: This page explains how to use Kubernetes API objects to define custom resources, allowing you to extend the built-in API without building a full custom server.

daemonset.md.title: DaemonSet
daemonset.md.summary: A Kubernetes DaemonSet ensures pods run on all nodes in a cluster, automatically scaling with node additions and removals. It is used for cluster storage, logs collection, and monitoring, with a spec containing a pod template with a specific restart policy.

debug-application.md.title: Troubleshooting Applications
debug-application.md.summary: This guide provides resources for fixing issues with containerized applications, covering common Kubernetes resource problems, container termination messages, and debugging running containers.

debug-cluster-windows.md.title: Windows debugging tips
debug-cluster-windows.md.summary: This page provides troubleshooting steps for Windows debugging issues, including resolving container creation errors, ensuring node compatibility, and configuring network settings like MAC spoofing and ICMP rules for Windows Pods.

debug-cluster.md.title: Troubleshooting Clusters
debug-cluster.md.summary: This guide explains how to diagnose and resolve cluster issues using kubectl commands, focusing on verifying node registration, checking cluster health via cluster-info, and inspecting specific nodes for status and events.

debug-init-containers.md.title: Debug Init Containers
debug-init-containers.md.summary: This page explains how to investigate execution problems in Init Containers using kubectl commands like `kubectl get pod`, `kubectl describe pod`, and `kubectl logs` to monitor container states, restart counts, and logs.

debug-pods.md.title: Debug Pods
debug-pods.md.summary: This guide explains how to diagnose and troubleshoot Kubernetes Pods that are stuck in states like Pending, Waiting, or Terminating, including resource exhaustion, image pull failures, and finalizer/admission webhook issues.

debug-running-pod.md.title: Debug Running Pods
debug-running-pod.md.summary: This page explains how to debug Pods running on a Node, including how to use `kubectl describe pod` to fetch details about pods and their status.

debug-service.md.title: Debug Services
debug-service.md.summary: This guide explains how to run interactive busybox Pods in Kubernetes to inspect service logs and diagnose issues when a Service is not responding to requests.

debug-statefulset.md.title: Debug a StatefulSet
debug-statefulset.md.summary: This task guides you on how to debug a StatefulSet by listing pods with a specific label, handling Unknown or Terminating states, and using the Debugging Pods guide for individual pod troubleshooting.

debug.md.title: Monitoring, Logging, and Debugging
debug.md.summary: This guide provides four sections for Kubernetes administrators: debugging applications, managing cluster issues, configuring Kubernetes logging, and enabling monitoring in Kubernetes clusters.

declarative-config.md.title: Declarative Management of Kubernetes Objects Using Configuration Files
declarative-config.md.summary: This guide explains how to create, update, and delete Kubernetes objects by storing configuration files in a directory and using `kubectl apply`. It details the trade-offs between imperative and declarative methods, defines terms like live objects and writers, and provides shell commands for creating objects with annotations.

declare-network-policy.md.title: Declare Network Policy
declare-network-policy.md.summary: This guide explains how to configure Kubernetes Network Policies using the API to control pod communication between services like nginx, covering deployment setup, service creation, and policy assignment for access control.

decrypt-data.md.title: Decrypting At-Rest Encrypted Kubernetes API Data
decrypt-data.md.summary: This guide explains how to switch from at-rest encryption to unencrypted API data storage in Kubernetes, specifically for Secrets and custom resources, while noting that etcd v3.x and Kubernetes v1.26+ are required for this operation.

define-command-argument-container.md.title: Define a Command and Arguments for a Container
define-command-argument-container.md.summary: This page explains how to define commands and arguments for containerized pods using the `command` and `args` fields in YAML configuration files, including shell script execution and environment variable substitution.

define-environment-variable-container.md.title: Define Environment Variables for a Container
define-environment-variable-container.md.summary: This page explains how to define environment variables for Kubernetes Pod containers using the `env` and `envFrom` fields, allowing you to inject values from ConfigMaps or Secrets into container configurations.

define-environment-variable-via-file.md.title: Define Environment Variable Values Using An Init Container
define-environment-variable-via-file.md.summary: This page explains how to configure environment variables for containers in a Pod via file, specifically focusing on the `initContainer` that mounts an emptyDir volume and writes variables to a file. It details the `fileKeyRef` field and the `optional` setting, while noting that `emptyDir` volumes lack security protections compared to Secret objects.

define-interdependent-environment-variab.title: Define Dependent Environment Variables
define-interdependent-environment-variab.summary: This page explains how to create Kubernetes Pods with dependent environment variables using the $(VAR_NAME) syntax in the env field, detailing dependency resolution rules and escaping techniques.

delete-stateful-set.md.title: Delete a StatefulSet
delete-stateful-set.md.summary: This guide explains how to delete a StatefulSet in Kubernetes using kubectl, including proper handling of pods and PersistentVolumes to prevent data loss during deletion.

deploy-intro.md.title: Using kubectl to Create a Deployment
deploy-intro.md.summary: This guide explains how to deploy applications on Kubernetes using kubectl, covering deployment creation, container image selection, and replica count configuration.

deployment.md.title: Deployments
deployment.md.summary: This page explains how Kubernetes Deployments provide declarative updates for Pods and ReplicaSets, allowing controlled rollouts, rollbacks, and scaling of containerized applications.

determine-reason-pod-failure.md.title: Determine the Reason for Pod Failure
determine-reason-pod-failure.md.summary: This page explains how to write and read Kubernetes termination messages for containers, including how to use Go templates to filter logs and customize the message path for different log files.

developing-cloud-controller-manager.md.title: Developing Cloud Controller Manager
developing-cloud-controller-manager.md.summary: This guide explains how to build out-of-tree cloud controller managers by following a template in Kubernetes core's main.go, importing a cloud provider package, and registering providers via the cloudprovider.RegisterCloudProvider function.

device-plugin-api-versions.md.title: Kubelet Device Manager API Versions
device-plugin-api-versions.md.summary: This page details version compatibility between the Kubernetes device plugin API and different Kubernetes versions, showing which versions support each API version (v1alpha1, v1beta1) and which have removed features.

device-plugin.md.title: Device Plugin
device-plugin.md.summary: Device plugins allow Kubernetes workloads to access hardware resources on specific nodes by advertising them to the kubelet, enabling vendor-specific initialization.

device-plugins.md.title: Device Plugins
device-plugins.md.summary: Kubernetes provides a device plugin framework allowing vendors to deploy hardware resources (like GPUs) to kubelets. Plugins register via gRPC, manage their own Unix sockets, and advertise these resources to the API server for scheduling.

device-taints.md.title: Device Taints and Tolerations
device-taints.md.summary: This page explains device taints and tolerations in DRA, detailing how drivers and admins can prevent Pods from scheduling on tainted devices, how tolerations allow resource claims to ignore taints, and the mechanisms for delaying or evicting pods.

device.md.title: Device
device.md.summary: This page defines devices as infrastructure resources attached to nodes, including commercial products like GPUs and custom hardware like ASIC boards, which require device drivers for Kubernetes Pods to access.

deviceclass.md.title: DeviceClass
deviceclass.md.summary: This page explains how administrators define DeviceClasses to claim and utilize dynamic resource allocation (DRA) within a cluster.

disruption-and-priority.md.title: Pod Group Disruption and Priority
disruption-and-priority.md.summary: This page explains how PodGroup can declare disruption modes (Single/All) and priority, detailing how these settings affect scheduler behavior during preemption events and how they interact with PriorityClasses.

disruption.md.title: Disruption
disruption.md.summary: This page explains Kubernetes concepts regarding disruptions, distinguishing between voluntary and involuntary disruptions caused by Pod failures or node outages, and how they impact workload management resources.

disruptions.md.title: Disruptions
disruptions.md.summary: This guide explains involuntary and voluntary disruptions in Kubernetes Pods, covering causes like hardware failures and node evictions, and provides strategies to mitigate them.

distribute-credentials-secure.md.title: Distribute Credentials Securely Using Secrets
distribute-credentials-secure.md.summary: This guide explains how to securely inject sensitive data like passwords and encryption keys into Kubernetes Pods using base64 encoding and Kubernetes Secrets, offering both manual and automated kubectl methods.

dns-custom-nameservers.md.title: Customizing DNS Service
dns-custom-nameservers.md.summary: This page explains how to configure your Kubernetes cluster's CoreDNS add-on and customize the DNS resolution process for your pods and services.

dns-debugging-resolution.md.title: Debugging DNS Resolution
dns-debugging-resolution.md.summary: This page guides users on diagnosing DNS problems by configuring CoreDNS, verifying the pod status, and checking local resolv.conf settings to ensure services like kubernetes.default resolve correctly.

dns-horizontal-autoscaling.md.title: Enable and Configure DNS Horizontal Autoscaling in Kubernetes
dns-horizontal-autoscaling.md.summary: This guide explains how to enable and tune DNS horizontal autoscaling in a Kubernetes cluster by creating a Deployment named 'kube-dns-autoscaler' and modifying the kube-dns-autoscaler ConfigMap.

dns-pod-service.md.title: Kubernetes DNS for Services and Pods
dns-pod-service.md.summary: This page explains how Kubernetes creates DNS records for Services and Pods, allowing pods to resolve services by name rather than IP addresses. It details how namespaces affect query results and how DNS queries can be expanded using the Pod's resolv.conf file.

docker.md.title: Docker
docker.md.summary: Docker Engine provides OS-level virtualization using Linux kernel features like cgroups and namespaces to isolate containers within a single Linux instance, avoiding VM overhead.

dockershim.md.title: Dockershim
dockershim.md.summary: Dockershim is a Kubernetes component that enables kubelets to communicate with Docker Engine. Starting with version 1.24, it was removed from Kubernetes.

downstream.md.title: Downstream (disambiguation)
downstream.md.summary: This page explains the technical distinction between 'downstream' and 'upstream' in the Kubernetes ecosystem, where downstream refers to code or tools relying on the core Kubernetes codebase, while upstream refers to the original source repository.

downward-api-volume-expose-pod-informati.title: Expose Pod Information to Containers Through Files
downward-api-volume-expose-pod-informati.summary: This page explains how Kubernetes pods can use a downward API volume to expose their metadata (labels and annotations) to running containers via file mounts, as opposed to environment variables.

downward-api.md.title: Downward API
downward-api.md.summary: This documentation explains the Downward API, a mechanism allowing containers to consume information about themselves or the cluster without relying on Kubernetes client APIs. It details how to expose Pod and container fields via environment variables or `downwardAPI` volumes, specifically focusing on fields like `metadata.name`, `metadata.labels`, and `metadata.uid`.

dra-api.md.title: DRA API Objects
dra-api.md.summary: This page describes Kubernetes API kinds used by Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) to categorize, request, and allocate devices. It details DeviceClass, ResourceClaims, and ResourceClaimTemplates, explaining how these components work together to manage device allocation within the cluster.

dra-features.md.title: DRA Features
dra-features.md.summary: This page describes optional DRA features for advanced use cases, detailing partitionable devices and device compatibility groups that allow logical devices to consume resources from shared physical devices.

dra-observability.md.title: Observability of Dynamic Resources
dra-observability.md.summary: This page explains how to monitor the status and health of dynamically allocated resources managed by DRA, including kubelet device metrics, ResourceClaim device status, and device health monitoring.

dra-standard-device-attributes.md.title: Standard Device Attributes for Dynamic Resource Allocation
dra-standard-device-attributes.md.summary: Kubernetes defines standard device attributes (like NUMA nodes and PCI bus IDs) for Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) drivers to enable cross-device matching without requiring driver-specific knowledge.

dra.md.title: Good Practices for Dynamic Resource Allocation as a Cluster Admin
dra.md.summary: This page outlines best practices for configuring Kubernetes clusters using Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA), including managing separate permissions for DRA APIs, deploying and maintaining DRA drivers, and ensuring seamless upgrades to minimize scheduling delays.

drain.md.title: kubectl drain
drain.md.summary: The command to safely evict Pods from a Node to prepare it for maintenance or removal from a cluster.

dual-stack-support.md.title: Dual-stack support with kubeadm
dual-stack-support.md.summary: This page explains how to configure Kubernetes clusters for dual-stack networking, allowing pods and services to use both IPv4 and IPv6 address families. It details prerequisites like enabling IPv6 packet forwarding via sysctl, provides examples of kubeadm init commands with specific address ranges, and shows how to configure the kubeadm configuration file for primary nodes.

dual-stack.md.title: IPv4/IPv6 dual-stack networking
dual-stack.md.summary: This page explains how Kubernetes clusters can allocate both IPv4 and IPv6 addresses to Pods and Services, enabling dual-stack networking by default starting in Kubernetes 1.21.

duration.md.title: Duration
duration.md.summary: This page explains how to represent time durations in Kubernetes, specifically using Go's time.Duration type and valid units like seconds, minutes, and hours.

dynamic-provisioning.md.title: Dynamic Volume Provisioning
dynamic-provisioning.md.summary: This page explains how cluster administrators can automatically provision storage volumes on-demand using StorageClass objects, eliminating the need for manual volume creation calls. It details the process of defining provisioners and parameters for volumes, and notes that the `storageClassName` field in PersistentVolumeClaims must match the configured StorageClass name.

dynamic-resource-allocation.md.title: Dynamic Resource Allocation
dynamic-resource-allocation.md.summary: This page explains Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) in Kubernetes, detailing how it allows flexible device provisioning by using PersistentVolumeClaims to claim storage and request capacity for Pods. It highlights benefits like flexible filtering, device sharing, and centralized categorization, contrasting DRA with device plugins that require per-container requests.

dynamic-volume-provisioning.md.title: Dynamic Volume Provisioning
dynamic-volume-provisioning.md.summary: This page explains how users can request automatic storage volume creation via an API, eliminating the need for cluster administrators to pre-provision storage.

enable-disable-api.md.title: Enable or Disable Kubernetes API Version
enable-disable-api.md.summary: This page explains how to enable or disable specific API versions from a Kubernetes cluster's control plane using the `--runtime-config` command-line argument.

encrypt-data.md.title: Encrypting Confidential Data at Rest
encrypt-data.md.summary: This page explains how to enable and configure at-rest encryption for Kubernetes API data, specifically for Secrets and custom resources. It details prerequisites like Kubernetes v1.26+ and etcd v3.x, and provides configuration examples for the `Identity` provider to ensure data confidentiality.

endpoint-slice.md.title: EndpointSlices
endpoint-slice.md.summary: EndpointSlices track backend IP addresses for services, typically backing Pods in Kubernetes. They are managed automatically by the control plane but can be defined manually for services without selectors.

endpoint-slices.md.title: EndpointSlices API
endpoint-slices.md.summary: This page explains Kubernetes EndpointSlices, which are network endpoints managed by the control plane for Kubernetes Services. They group endpoints by IP family, protocol, port, and service name, defaulting to 100 endpoints per slice. The page details how these slices serve as the source of truth for kube-proxy traffic routing, support IPv4 and IPv6, and include conditions like serving, terminating, and ready.

endpoint.md.title: Endpoints API
endpoint.md.summary: Deprecated Kubernetes API for service endpoints, replaced by Endpointslices starting v1.21.

enforce-standards-admission-controller.m.title: Enforce Pod Security Standards by Configuring the Built-in Admission Controller
enforce-standards-admission-controller.m.summary: This page explains how to configure Kubernetes's built-in admission controller to enforce Pod Security Standards, including version-specific configurations for v1.22, v1.23, and v1.24, as well as setting cluster-wide defaults and exemptions.

enforce-standards-namespace-labels.md.title: Enforce Pod Security Standards with Namespace Labels
enforce-standards-namespace-labels.md.summary: This guide explains how to enforce Pod Security Standards using namespace labels, including policies like `baseline` and `restricted`, and how to apply them via `kubectl label` with `--dry-run` for testing.

enforcing-pod-security-standards.md.title: Enforcing Pod Security Standards
enforcing-pod-security-standards.md.summary: This page outlines best practices for enforcing Pod Security Standards, including configuring the Pod Security Admission Controller, applying least privilege principles, and using audit/warn modes to manage namespace security levels.

environment-variable-expose-pod-informat.title: Expose Pod Information to Containers Through Environment Variables
environment-variable-expose-pod-informat.summary: This page explains how Kubernetes Pods can use environment variables to expose their own fields (like pod name, namespace, IP address) to running containers via the downward API, enabling runtime discovery of services.

ephemeral-container.md.title: Ephemeral Container
ephemeral-container.md.summary: Ephemeral containers are temporary pods used for diagnostic purposes within a pod, lacking resource guarantees and not suitable for running workload components themselves.

ephemeral-containers.md.title: Ephemeral Containers
ephemeral-containers.md.summary: Ephemeral containers are temporary, non-restartable containers used for troubleshooting by inspecting existing pods without rebuilding applications. They lack resource guarantees and are incompatible with static pods, making them ideal for debugging issues where `kubectl exec` fails.

ephemeral-storage.md.title: Local Ephemeral Storage
ephemeral-storage.md.summary: This page explains how Kubernetes nodes use local storage (emptyDir, writable layers, logs) for scratch space and caching, noting that data is not guaranteed durable and that resource quotas must be configured per namespace and pod to enforce limits.

ephemeral-volumes.md.title: Ephemeral Volumes in Kubernetes
ephemeral-volumes.md.summary: This document explains ephemeral volumes in Kubernetes, which are temporary storage volumes created and deleted with pods to allow applications to cache data without requiring persistent storage across restarts.

etcd.md.title: etcd
etcd.md.summary: etcd is a consistent and highly-available key-value store used as Kubernetes' backing store for cluster data. It requires a backup plan for data if the cluster uses it.

event.md.title: Event in Kubernetes
event.md.summary: Kubernetes objects that track state changes or notable cluster occurrences. Events are best-effort data with limited retention, requiring consumers to avoid timing assumptions based on event reasons or event persistence.

eviction.md.title: Eviction
eviction.md.summary: This page explains how Pods are terminated on Nodes, detailing two types of eviction: Node-pressure eviction and API-initiated eviction.

explore-intro.md.title: Viewing Pods and Nodes
explore-intro.md.summary: This page explains Kubernetes Pods (atomic application containers) and Nodes (worker machines managed by the control plane), detailing how Pods share resources like storage and networking while Nodes host them.

expose-external-ip-address.md.title: Exposing an External IP Address to Access an Application in a Cluster
expose-external-ip-address.md.summary: This guide demonstrates how to create a Kubernetes LoadBalancer Service that exposes an external IP address to access a running application running in five pods.

expose-intro.md.title: Using a Service to Expose Your App
expose-intro.md.summary: This tutorial explains how to use a Service in Kubernetes to expose an application outside a cluster, covering clusterIP, nodePort, and loadBalancer types.

extend-kubernetes.md.title: Extending Kubernetes
extend-kubernetes.md.summary: This guide explains how to customize Kubernetes clusters by covering configuration options (command-line args, local files) and extensions (running additional programs/services), with a focus on extensions as the primary approach for cluster operators.

extend-service-ip-ranges.md.title: Extend Service IP Ranges
extend-service-ip-ranges.md.summary: This guide explains how to extend the Service IP range assigned to a Kubernetes cluster using the `--service-cluster-ip-range` command-line argument. It details the process of adding new ServiceCIDRs to increase available addresses, specifically addressing the limitation where the default Service consumes the full range, leaving only 13 services for 14 IPs.

extended-resource-node.md.title: Advertise Extended Resources for a Node
extended-resource-node.md.summary: This page explains how to specify node-level extended resources (like dongles) that Kubernetes does not know about, allowing applications to request these resources via HTTP PATCH requests.

extended-resource.md.title: Assign Extended Resources to a Container
extended-resource.md.summary: This page explains how to assign extended resources (like dongles) to Kubernetes containers by configuring the `resources.requests` field in pod manifests. It details the process of scheduling pods that request more resources than available on the node, including the difference between Node-advertised capacity and Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA).

extensible-admission-controllers.md.title: Dynamic Admission Control
extensible-admission-controllers.md.summary: This page explains how to build, configure, and monitor Kubernetes admission webhooks, which are HTTP callbacks that validate or modify API server requests to enforce custom policies.

extensions.md.title: Extensions
extensions.md.summary: This page explains how Kubernetes extensions allow administrators to deploy custom software components that integrate deeply with the cluster, reducing the need for manual installation.

feature-gates.md.title: Feature Gate
feature-gates.md.summary: Feature gates are opaque keys used to control which Kubernetes features are enabled in a cluster, allowing you to selectively activate or deactivate specific features per component.

field-selectors.md.title: Field Selectors
field-selectors.md.summary: This page explains how to use Kubernetes field selectors to filter Kubernetes resources (like Pods) by specific values in metadata or status fields, providing examples and supported field types.

finalizer.md.title: Kubernetes Finalizer
finalizer.md.summary: Kubernetes uses finalizers to wait for specific cleanup conditions before deleting resources marked for deletion. This allows the control plane to clean up related resources like API or infrastructure before the main deletion process completes.

finalizers.md.title: Finalizers
finalizers.md.summary: Kubernetes finalizers control garbage collection by allowing controllers to remove specific keys from a resource's metadata before deletion, preventing accidental removal of resources like PersistentVolumes until their lifecycle ends.

find-out-runtime-you-use.md.title: Find Out What Container Runtime is Used on a Node
find-out-runtime-you-use.md.summary: This page guides users on how to identify the container runtime (e.g., Docker Engine, containerd) and its version on Kubernetes nodes using the `kubectl get nodes` command, which outputs the `CONTAINER-RUNTIME` column.

fine-parallel-processing-work-queue.md.title: Fine Parallel Processing Using a Work Queue
fine-parallel-processing-work-queue.md.summary: This guide explains how to run a Kubernetes Job that uses Redis as a work queue to execute multiple parallel tasks across worker pods. It details the setup steps including starting Redis, creating a queue, and initializing a custom work-queue client library.

flexvolume.md.title: FlexVolume
flexvolume.md.summary: Deprecated interface for out-of-tree volume plugins in Kubernetes, replaced by the Container Storage Interface (CSI) which requires root access and addresses limitations of FlexVolume.

flow-control.md.title: API Priority and Fairness
flow-control.md.summary: This page explains how the Kubernetes API server controls request behavior during high traffic, specifically detailing the APF feature that classifies and isolates requests to prevent overload and crashes. It contrasts the default `--max-requests-inflight` limit with the APF feature, which uses a fine-grained queue and fair queuing to ensure critical requests are prioritized even when other requests are delayed.

force-delete-stateful-set-pod.md.title: Force Delete StatefulSet Pods
force-delete-stateful-set-pod.md.summary: This page explains how to safely delete pods within a StatefulSet, emphasizing that manual deletion is unsafe due to the 'at most one' semantics. It details the correct command (kubectl delete pods) and warns against setting termination grace period to zero, which can cause pods to be deleted by the kubelet instead of the user.

gang-scheduling.md.title: Gang Scheduling
gang-scheduling.md.summary: Gang scheduling ensures Pods are scheduled on an all-or-nothing basis. If the cluster cannot accommodate the entire group, none are bound to nodes. It relies on the PodGroup API and ensures the minCount constraint is met by checking if scheduled Pods plus newly feasible unscheduled Pods reach the threshold.

garbage-collection.md.title: Garbage Collection
garbage-collection.md.summary: Kubernetes's garbage collection mechanism allows the control plane to clean up resources like terminated pods, completed jobs, and unused containers by verifying their owners and dependents before deletion.

gateway.md.title: Gateway API
gateway.md.summary: Gateway API is an extensible, role-oriented configuration mechanism that enables dynamic infrastructure provisioning and advanced traffic routing for Kubernetes clusters.

get-shell-running-container.md.title: Get a Shell to a Running Container
get-shell-running-container.md.summary: This page explains how to use `kubectl exec` to run a shell inside a running container, including arguments like `--stdin` and `--tty`, and how to handle multiple containers using the `-i` and `-c` flags.

glossary-api-eviction.md.title: API-initiated eviction
glossary-api-eviction.md.summary: This page explains how to use the Kubernetes API to create an Eviction object that triggers graceful pod termination via the kube-apiserver, respecting PodDisruptionBudgets and termination grace periods.

glossary-configmap.md.title: ConfigMap
glossary-configmap.md.summary: A Kubernetes API object storing non-confidential data in key-value pairs, enabling pods to use environment variables, command-line arguments, or volume files for configuration.

glossary-container-lifecycle-hooks.md.title: Container Lifecycle Hooks
glossary-container-lifecycle-hooks.md.summary: This page explains how containers can run code at specific moments in their lifecycle, specifically PostStart (immediately after creation) and PreStop (immediately before termination).

glossary-controller.md.title: Kubernetes Controller
glossary-controller.md.summary: Kubernetes controllers are control loops that monitor cluster state and make changes to align it with desired state, running within the control plane.

glossary-cri.md.title: Container Runtime Interface (CRI) Protocol
glossary-cri.md.summary: The CRI defines the gRPC protocol for communication between kubelets and container runtime, enabling efficient inter-component communication.

glossary-deployment.md.title: Deployment
glossary-deployment.md.summary: This page explains how to deploy replicated applications using Pods without local state, detailing the architecture where pods are distributed across cluster nodes.

glossary-downward-api.md.title: Downward API
glossary-downward-api.md.summary: Kubernetes mechanism to expose Pod and container fields to code running in a container, allowing applications to access cluster information without modifying their own code.

glossary-dra.md.title: Dynamic Resource Allocation
glossary-dra.md.summary: Kubernetes feature allowing workload requests to share hardware accelerators across pods by defining device classes and assigning them to specific claims on nodes.

glossary-garbage-collection.md.title: Garbage Collection
glossary-garbage-collection.md.summary: Kubernetes uses garbage collection to clean up cluster resources like unused containers, failed pods, and expired objects.

glossary-kube-scheduler.md.title: kube-scheduler
glossary-kube-scheduler.md.summary: The kube-scheduler is a control plane component that selects nodes for newly created Pods by considering resource requirements, hardware constraints, and affinity policies.

glossary-kubectl.md.title: Kubectl
glossary-kubectl.md.summary: Kubectl is a command-line tool for communicating with a Kubernetes cluster's control plane using the Kubernetes API.

glossary-kubernetes-api.md.title: Kubernetes API
glossary-kubernetes-api.md.summary: The HTTP API that enables users, cluster components, and external systems to communicate with Kubernetes objects and query their state via RESTful calls.

glossary-logging.md.title: Logging
glossary-logging.md.summary: This page explains how logs are generated by cluster and applications, detailing their purpose for debugging and monitoring cluster activity.

glossary-mixed-version-proxy.md.title: Mixed Version Proxy (MVP)
glossary-mixed-version-proxy.md.summary: This feature allows a kube-apiserver to proxy resource requests to a different peer API server, enabling correct resource serving when multiple Kubernetes API servers run different versions.

glossary-node-pressure-eviction.md.title: Node-pressure eviction
glossary-node-pressure-eviction.md.summary: The kubelet proactively terminates pods to reclaim resources on nodes when CPU, memory, or disk space reaches specific consumption levels to prevent starvation.

glossary-pod-lifecycle.md.title: Pod Lifecycle
glossary-pod-lifecycle.md.summary: This page defines the five phases a Pod passes through during its lifetime: Pending, Running, Succeeded, Failed, and Unknown. It explains that the `phase` field in the PodStatus API represents this state.

glossary-pod-security-policy.md.title: Pod Security Policy
glossary-pod-security-policy.md.summary: A deprecated Kubernetes API for enforcing security restrictions during pod creation and updates, now replaced by Pod Security Admission and third-party plugins.

glossary-secret.md.title: Secrets
glossary-secret.md.summary: Secrets store sensitive data like passwords and tokens, allowing granular control over encryption and usage. They are encoded as base64 and stored unencrypted by default, with encryption options available for production environments.

glossary-security-context.md.title: Security Context
glossary-security-context.md.summary: This page explains how to configure privilege and access control settings for Pods and containers, including defining users, groups, and security policies like SELinux or AppArmor.

glossary-service.md.title: Kubernetes Service
glossary-service.md.summary: This page explains how Kubernetes exposes network applications running as Pods, detailing the selector-based pod set, IP networking capabilities, and its role in enabling services like Ingress and Gateways.

glossary-statefulset.md.title: StatefulSet
glossary-statefulset.md.summary: A Kubernetes resource that manages Pods with guaranteed ordering and uniqueness, maintaining sticky identities across rescheduling. It enables persistent storage volumes for workloads by ensuring pods are matched to existing volumes.

group-version-resource.md.title: Group Version Resource
group-version-resource.md.summary: GVRs define Kubernetes APIs by specifying the group, version, and resource name, enabling stable access to objects even as APIs change.

guaranteed-scheduling-critical-addon-pod.title: Guaranteed Scheduling For Critical Add-On Pods
guaranteed-scheduling-critical-addon-pod.summary: This guide explains how to ensure critical add-on pods (like metrics-server, DNS, and UI) are never evicted from a Kubernetes cluster, preventing cluster failures. It details the method of setting priorityClassName to `system-cluster-critical` or `system-node-critical` to prevent permanent pod eviction.

guestbook.md.title: Deploying PHP Guestbook application with Redis
guestbook.md.summary: This guide demonstrates how to build and deploy a multi-tier web application using Kubernetes and Docker, specifically focusing on deploying a Redis leader service, managing Redis followers, and setting up the guestbook frontend.

ha-topology.md.title: Options for Highly Available Topology
ha-topology.md.summary: This page explains two HA cluster configurations: stacked etcd topology (default) and external etcd topology, detailing how etcd nodes are distributed relative to control plane nodes and their impact on redundancy.

hardening-dra.md.title: Harden Dynamic Resource Allocation in Your Cluster
hardening-dra.md.summary: This guide details how to harden authorization for Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) in Kubernetes, focusing on least-privilege access for ResourceClaim status updates. It covers identifying writers, granting synthetic subresource permissions, and binding roles to specific ServiceAccounts.

hardening-guide-dynamic-resource-allocat.title: Hardening Guide - Dynamic Resource Allocation
hardening-guide-dynamic-resource-allocat.summary: This guide explains how to harden DRA (Dynamic Resource Allocation) status updates by enforcing least-privilege RBAC. It details the two synthetic subresources (binding and driver) required for scheduler and driver updates, and provides specific RBAC patterns for node-local and multi-node controllers to ensure only necessary components can modify resource claims.

hello-minikube.md.title: Hello Minikube Tutorial
hello-minikube.md.summary: This page guides users on running a sample application on a minikube Kubernetes cluster, covering deployment, running, and logging. It assumes prior setup of minikube and kubectl and provides commands to verify cluster status, access the dashboard, and create deployments.

helm-chart.md.title: Helm Chart
helm-chart.md.summary: Helm is a package of pre-configured Kubernetes configurations that enables reproducible deployment of applications, allowing users to manage charts for deployment.

high-availability.md.title: Creating Highly Available Clusters with kubeadm
high-availability.md.summary: This guide explains two kubeadm deployment strategies for Kubernetes: stacked control plane nodes (co-located, less infrastructure) versus external etcd clusters (separated, more infrastructure). It details prerequisites like network connectivity and container runtime setup, and warns against using this approach in cloud environments with specific service object limitations.

horizontal-pod-autoscale-walkthrough.md.title: HorizontalPodAutoscaler Walkthrough
horizontal-pod-autoscale-walkthrough.md.summary: This guide demonstrates how to enable and deploy a HorizontalPodAutoscaler (HPA) in Kubernetes to automatically scale a PHP web application based on load metrics. It covers prerequisites like a Metrics Server, deploying a Deployment and Service, and configuring the HPA controller to adjust pod counts dynamically.

horizontal-pod-autoscale.md.title: Horizontal Pod Autoscaling
horizontal-pod-autoscale.md.summary: Kubernetes's HPA automatically scales Deployment/StatefulSet pods to match load by adjusting desired scale based on CPU/memory metrics, unlike vertical scaling which adds resources.

horizontal-pod-autoscaler.md.title: Horizontal Pod Autoscaler
horizontal-pod-autoscaler.md.summary: HPA automatically adjusts pod replica counts based on resource utilization or custom metrics, typically used with Deployments or ReplicaSets.

host-aliases.md.title: HostAliases
host-aliases.md.summary: Maps IP addresses to hostnames for injecting into Pod hosts files, valid only for non-hostNetwork Pods.

how-dra-works.md.title: How DRA Works
how-dra-works.md.summary: This page explains how Kubernetes allocates devices to workloads using dynamic resource allocation (DRA), detailing the driver creation, cluster configuration, and workflow for ResourceSlices and Pods.

http-proxy-access-api.md.title: HTTP Proxy for Kubernetes API Access
http-proxy-access-api.md.summary: This guide explains how to use an HTTP proxy to access the Kubernetes API server via kubectl proxy, providing examples for starting the proxy and exploring API endpoints like API versions and pods.

image-volumes.md.title: Use an Image Volume With a Pod
image-volumes.md.summary: This guide explains how to configure a pod using OCI image volumes, allowing you to mount content from OCI registries inside containers. It covers prerequisites like container runtime support and host exec capabilities, followed by step-by-step instructions for creating and attaching pods with image volumes, including examples for standard paths and subPath usage.

image.md.title: Image
image.md.summary: This page explains how images are stored in container registries, how they are pulled to local systems, and how they run as applications with associated metadata.

images.md.title: Container Images
images.md.summary: This page outlines the concept of container images, which are executable software bundles with runtime assumptions. It details how images are named (including tags and digests), how they are pushed to registries, and how Kubernetes uses them in pods.

immutable-infrastructure.md.title: Immutable Infrastructure
immutable-infrastructure.md.summary: Immutable infrastructure describes computer systems that cannot be changed once deployed, enforced by automated overwriting mechanisms, and relies on version control for durable audit logs.

imperative-command.md.title: Managing Kubernetes Objects Using Imperative Commands
imperative-command.md.summary: This guide explains how to create, update, and delete Kubernetes objects directly using imperative commands like `kubectl create`, `kubectl set`, and `kubectl edit`. It details how to use verb-driven commands for common object types such as Pods, Services, and Autoscalers, along with the trade-offs between imperative and declarative approaches.

imperative-config.md.title: Kubernetes Object Management Guide
imperative-config.md.summary: This guide explains how to create, update, and delete Kubernetes objects using the `kubectl` command-line tool and YAML/JSON configuration files, including trade-offs between imperative and declarative approaches.

indexed-parallel-processing-static.md.title: Indexed Job for Parallel Processing with Static Work Assignment
indexed-parallel-processing-static.md.summary: This documentation explains how to run a Kubernetes Job using the 'Indexed' completion mode, where each worker pod is assigned a specific index based on its position in the task. The control plane automatically sets a downward API environment variable to expose this index, allowing the containerized task to know which part of the overall work item to execute.

infrastructure-resource.md.title: Kubernetes Resource Management
infrastructure-resource.md.summary: This page explains how Kubernetes manages and allocates CPU, memory, and other hardware resources across nodes and pods, utilizing cgroups and dynamic allocation mechanisms.

ingress-controllers.md.title: Ingress Controllers
ingress-controllers.md.summary: This page details Kubernetes support for AWS, GCE, and various third-party ingress controllers including AKS, Alibaba Cloud, Apache APISIX, and Citrix, noting that the Ingress API is frozen and deprecated.

ingress.md.title: Ingress API Reference
ingress.md.summary: This page explains the Kubernetes Ingress API, its deprecation status, and provides terminology for cluster networking concepts like nodes, clusters, and edge routers.

init-container.md.title: Init Container
init-container.md.summary: Init containers are required before app containers to ensure all initialization tasks complete before the application starts. Unlike sidecar containers, they do not persist after pod startup.

init-containers.md.title: Init Containers
init-containers.md.summary: Init containers are specialized Kubernetes containers that run before app containers in a Pod, allowing utilities or setup scripts to be included in the image. They must complete successfully before the Pod can be ready, and if a failure occurs, kubelet restarts the container until it succeeds.

install-kubeadm.md.title: Installing kubeadm
install-kubeadm.md.summary: This page guides users on how to install the kubeadm toolbox, including requirements like RAM, CPU, and kernel compatibility, and verifies MAC addresses and product UUIDs for each node.

install-kubectl-linux.md.title: Install and Set Up kubectl on Linux
install-kubectl-linux.md.summary: This guide details how to install kubectl on Linux, covering both binary installation via curl and native package management, including version validation and installation steps.

install-kubectl-macos.md.title: Install and Set Up kubectl on macOS
install-kubectl-macos.md.summary: This guide details how to install kubectl on macOS using multiple methods including downloading binaries via curl, verifying versions, and configuring PATH and permissions.

install-kubectl-windows.md.title: Install and Set Up kubectl on Windows
install-kubectl-windows.md.summary: This guide details two methods for installing kubectl on Windows: downloading the binary directly via direct download or curl, and installing it using Chocolatey, Scoop, or winget.

install-use-dra.md.title: Install Drivers and Allocate Devices with DRA
install-use-dra.md.summary: This tutorial guides administrators on installing Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) drivers and using them with Kubernetes APIs to allocate devices to Pods. It covers deploying drivers, creating Pod claims, and managing cluster state.

intro.md.title: Windows Containers in Kubernetes
intro.md.summary: This guide explains how to orchestrate Windows applications within Kubernetes clusters, detailing the requirements for Windows nodes (Windows Server 2022/2025), the limitations regarding Hyper-V isolation and container runtime features, and how Windows pods map to Linux concepts like Pods.

ip-masq-agent.md.title: IP Masquerade Agent User Guide
ip-masq-agent.md.summary: This guide explains how to configure the ip-masq-agent to hide pod IP addresses behind the cluster node's IP address for traffic to external destinations, handling non-masquerade CIDRs like 10.0.0.0/8 and 172.16.0.0/12.

istio.md.title: Istio
istio.md.summary: Istio is an open platform for microservices integration and traffic management, acting as a service mesh that abstracts cluster management.

job-with-pod-to-pod-communication.md.title: Job with Pod-to-Pod Communication
job-with-pod-to-pod-communication.md.summary: This guide explains how to configure a Job in Indexed completion mode to use pod hostnames for inter-pod communication instead of IP addresses, enabling deterministic DNS-based networking without external API connections.

job.md.title: Jobs
job.md.summary: This page explains how Kubernetes Jobs create, track, and clean up Pods. It details the Job's retry logic, parallel execution capabilities, and scheduling options like CronJobs.

jwt.md.title: JSON Web Token (JWT)
jwt.md.summary: A secure digital token for authentication and authorization in cloud environments like Kubernetes, allowing entities to verify their identity and permissions.

kernel-version-requirements.md.title: Linux Kernel Version Requirements
kernel-version-requirements.md.summary: This page explains that kernel version numbers alone are insufficient for certain OS distributions, as maintainers often backport features to older kernels. It details specific sysctls and nftables proxy modes requiring modern kernels (e.g., 3.16+ for net.ipv4.ip_local_reserved_ports), and notes that older kernels like 5.4 are only acceptable for testing with specific kube-proxy settings.

kms-provider.md.title: KMS Provider Configuration Guide
kms-provider.md.summary: This page explains how to configure a Key Management Service (KMS) provider and plugin in Kubernetes to enable secret data encryption. It details the version requirements (KMS v2 vs v1), encryption mechanisms using DEKs and KEKs, and specific configuration steps for the KMS provider.

kops.md.title: kOps (Kubernetes Operations)
kops.md.summary: kOps is an automated provisioning system that handles production-grade Kubernetes clusters, cloud infrastructure, and OS deployments across multiple platforms.

kube-apiserver.md.title: Kubernetes API Server
kube-apiserver.md.summary: The Kubernetes API server is a critical component of the control plane that exposes the Kubernetes API, enabling applications to interact with the Kubernetes ecosystem.

kube-proxy.md.title: kube-proxy
kube-proxy.md.summary: kube-proxy is a Kubernetes network proxy that runs on each node to implement service concepts, maintaining network rules for Pod communication within and outside the cluster.

kube-router-network-policy.md.title: Kube-router for NetworkPolicy
kube-router-network-policy.md.summary: This page guides users on installing and configuring Kube-router, a Kubernetes addon that manages iptables rules and ipsets for Kubernetes NetworkPolicy, enabling the deployment of NetworkPolicy controllers.

kube-scheduler.md.title: Kubernetes Scheduler
kube-scheduler.md.summary: This page explains how Kubernetes' kube-scheduler selects and scores nodes to assign Pods to, detailing the filtering, scoring, and binding processes to ensure pods run on feasible nodes.

kube-state-metrics.md.title: Metrics for Kubernetes Object States
kube-state-metrics.md.summary: This page explains how to expose Kubernetes object states via the kube-state-metrics agent, detailing how to query cluster readiness, detect termination states, and set up Prometheus-based alerting for critical conditions like pods blocked in terminating states.

kubeadm-certs.md.title: Certificate Management with kubeadm
kubeadm-certs.md.summary: This guide explains how to manage certificate renewals and other tasks using kubeadm, including configuring encryption algorithms, setting validity periods, and handling external CA files.

kubeadm-reconfigure.md.title: Reconfiguring a kubeadm cluster
kubeadm-reconfigure.md.summary: This guide explains how to manually edit cluster objects and files on disk to reconfigure kubeadm components, noting that kubeadm does not support automated reconfiguration of deployed components.

kubeadm-upgrade.md.title: Kubeadm Cluster Upgrade Guide
kubeadm-upgrade.md.summary: This page details the process for upgrading Kubernetes clusters created with kubeadm from older versions to newer ones, including minor and patch releases. It outlines the high-level workflow of upgrading primary, additional, and worker nodes, emphasizes the importance of version matching and draining nodes during minor upgrades, and advises against swapping control plane nodes.

kubectl-convert-overview.md.title: kubectl-convert overview
kubectl-convert-overview.md.summary: A plugin for kubectl that converts Kubernetes manifests between different API versions, aiding migration to newer releases.

kubectl-node-debug.md.title: Debugging Kubernetes Nodes With Kubectl
kubectl-node-debug.md.summary: This page explains how to use the `kubectl debug node` command to create an interactive shell on a Kubernetes node, allowing you to gather logs and troubleshoot issues without SSH access.

kubectl-plugins.md.title: Extend kubectl with plugins
kubectl-plugins.md.summary: This guide explains how to install and write custom kubectl plugins that extend core commands like create, version, and attach, while warning about limitations where plugins cannot override existing commands.

kubectl-whats-next.md.title: What's Next?
kubectl-whats-next.md.summary: This page guides users through the K8s ecosystem, covering Kubectl usage, Minikube installation, cluster creation, application deployment, and access management.

kubectl.md.title: kubectl Command-Line Tool
kubectl.md.summary: The kubectl tool is the primary interface for creating, inspecting, and managing Kubernetes objects. It connects to the API server via kubeconfig files, handles authentication, and supports operations like deploying, inspecting, and debugging cluster state.

kubelet-authn-authz.md.title: Kubelet Authentication/Authorization
kubelet-authn-authz.md.summary: This document explains how to configure and use kubelet authentication (anonymous, X509, and bearer token) and authorization modes (AlwaysAllow, Webhook, and SubjectAccessReview) to control access to the kubelet's HTTPS endpoint.

kubelet-checkpoint-api.md.title: Kubelet Checkpoint API
kubelet-checkpoint-api.md.summary: This page explains how to create stateful checkpoint archives for containers, detailing the process of creating a tar archive of all memory pages, security implications for root-only access, and the specific HTTP POST endpoint required by the kubelet.

kubelet-config-directory-merging.md.title: Kubelet Configuration Directory Merging
kubelet-config-directory-merging.md.summary: This page explains how kubelet's --config-dir flag merges different YAML data types (singular, embedded structures, lists, and maps) to create a unified kubelet configuration, allowing specific overrides while preserving the rest of the file.
