kubelet-credential-provider.md.title: Configure a kubelet image credential provider
kubelet-credential-provider.md.summary: This guide explains how to configure the kubelet's image credential provider plugin mechanism, enabling dynamic credential retrieval via exec plugins starting from Kubernetes v1.20. It details requirements for API calls, short-lived credentials, and specific feature gates (KubeletServiceAccountTokenForCredentialProviders) to support service account tokens for image pulls.

kubelet-files.md.title: Local Files And Paths Used By The Kubelet
kubelet-files.md.summary: This document details the internal paths and files the kubelet reads and writes, including configuration files, certificates, manifests, and system files like cgroups. It explains how kubelet connects to the control plane and manages state via checkpoint files.

kubelet-in-userns.md.title: Running Kubernetes Node Components as a Non-root User
kubelet-in-userns.md.summary: This guide explains how to run Kubernetes Node components like kubelet and CRI without root privileges by using a user namespace, also known as rootless mode.

kubelet-integration.md.title: Configuring each kubelet in your cluster using kubeadm
kubelet-integration.md.summary: This guide explains how to configure each kubelet in a Kubernetes cluster using the kubeadm CLI tool, which decouples the daemon from the init process. It details how to propagate cluster-level settings (like subnet and DNS) to all kubelets via the KubeletConfiguration API, ensuring consistent behavior across the cluster.

kubelet-pods-api.md.title: Kubelet Pods API
kubelet-pods-api.md.summary: This documentation describes the Kubelet Pods API, which allows local Node components to query Pod information directly from the kubelet via a UNIX socket. It provides gRPC methods for listing, watching, and retrieving pods, with reliability ensured by local cache and reconciliation.

kubelet-standalone.md.title: Running Kubelet in Standalone Mode
kubelet-standalone.md.summary: This tutorial guides users on installing and configuring a standalone kubelet instance on Linux, including swap management and IPv4 packet forwarding settings, to run Kubernetes pods without a control plane.

kubelet-sync-loop.md.title: Kubelet Sync Loop
kubelet-sync-loop.md.summary: This page explains how the kubelet orchestrates Pod reconciliation by running a sync loop that polls the runtime (PLEG) to update Pod state, ensuring containers match the desired state defined in the Pod spec.

kubelet-tls-bootstrapping.md.title: TLS Bootstrapping
kubelet-tls-bootstrapping.md.summary: This guide explains how to initialize TLS client certificates for kubelets on Kubernetes worker nodes, enabling secure communication with the control plane.

kubelet.md.title: Kubelet
kubelet.md.summary: A node agent that ensures container health and runs Pod specifications, managing containers not created by Kubernetes.

kubernetes-api.md.title: The Kubernetes API
kubernetes-api.md.summary: This page explains Kubernetes' core control plane, detailing how the API server exposes HTTP APIs for querying and manipulating state objects like Pods and Namespaces. It describes two mechanisms for publishing API specifications: the Discovery API (for resource lists) and the Kubernetes OpenAPI Document (for full schemas), with the OpenAPI v3 being the preferred method for comprehensive access.

kubernetes-basics.md.title: Learn Kubernetes Basics
kubernetes-basics.md.summary: This tutorial guides users through the fundamentals of Kubernetes cluster orchestration, covering deployment, scaling, and debugging containerized applications.

kustomization.md.title: Kustomize: Declarative Management of Kubernetes Objects
kustomization.md.summary: Kustomize is a standalone tool for customizing Kubernetes objects via kustomization files, enabling the generation of ConfigMaps and Secrets from external sources like .properties or .env files.

label.md.title: Label
label.md.summary: Labels are key-value pairs attached to Pods used to organize and select subsets of objects.

labels-annotations-taints.md.title: Well-Known Labels, Annotations and Taints
labels-annotations-taints.md.summary: This document details Kubernetes labels, annotations, and taints used on API objects, including examples like `app.kubernetes.io/` and `apf.kubernetes.io/`, explaining their purpose for managing and automating workloads.

labels.md.title: Labels and Selectors
labels.md.summary: This page defines Kubernetes labels as key-value pairs attached to Pods, enabling efficient queries and watches. It explains how labels map organizational structures to system objects, allowing users to select subsets of objects without requiring clients to store mappings. The page details valid syntax, character sets, and reserved prefixes for core components.

learning-environment.md.title: Learning environment
learning-environment.md.summary: This page outlines various ways to set up and use Kubernetes environments for learning, including local options like Kind and Minikube, online playgrounds such as Killercoda, and production clusters like kubeadm.

leases.md.title: Kubernetes Leases
leases.md.summary: Kubernetes uses leases to coordinate shared resources like node heartbeats and leader elections. Leases are managed in the kube-node-lease namespace, allowing the control plane to determine node availability and ensure only one instance of components runs at a time.

lifecycle.md.title: CompositePodGroup Lifecycle
lifecycle.md.summary: This page explains how CompositePodGroup resources function within a multi-level PodGroup hierarchy, detailing their ownership by workload controllers, creation order (top-down), and critical limitations like consistent scheduler names and priority constraints that prevent unschedulable hierarchies.

limit-range.md.title: Limit Ranges
limit-range.md.summary: This page explains how administrators can restrict resource consumption and creation of cluster resources like CPU, memory, and storage within a namespace using Kubernetes resource quotas. It details how LimitRanges enforce minimum and maximum limits for Pods and PVCs, enforce request/limit ratios, and set default values for compute resources.

limit-storage-consumption.md.title: Limit Storage Consumption
limit-storage-consumption.md.summary: This page explains how to limit storage consumption in a namespace using LimitRange (max/min storage per PVC) and ResourceQuota (max PVC count and cumulative storage).

limitrange.md.title: LimitRange
limitrange.md.summary: Limits the quantity of API resources or infrastructure resources a container can consume within a namespace.

linux-kernel-security-constraints.md.title: Linux kernel security constraints for Pods and containers
linux-kernel-security-constraints.md.summary: This page details kernel features like seccomp, AppArmor, and SELinux used to harden Kubernetes workloads by restricting root privileges and defining security contexts in Pod manifests.

linux-security.md.title: Security For Linux Nodes
linux-security.md.summary: This page outlines security considerations and best practices for Linux nodes, specifically focusing on memory-backed volumes like tmpfs and secret volumes that may persist to persistent storage if swap is not properly configured or kernel versions are outdated.

list-all-running-container-images.md.title: kubectl List All Container Images Running in a Cluster
list-all-running-container-images.md.summary: This page explains how to use kubectl to list all Container images for Pods running in a cluster, including methods via jsonpath, range operations, and filtering by label or namespace.

local-debugging.md.title: Developing and debugging services locally using telepresence
local-debugging.md.summary: Telepresence is a tool that allows developers to run local debugging and development tools on a remote Kubernetes cluster by intercepting remote traffic, enabling full access to cluster resources like ConfigMaps and secrets.

logging-logging.md.title: Logging in Kubernetes
logging-logging.md.summary: This page explains how to collect, access, and analyze logs using built-in tools and popular logging stacks within Kubernetes.
topics: A Practical Guide to Kubernetes Logging

logging.md.title: Logging Architecture
logging.md.summary: This page explains how to manage and store application logs in Kubernetes, covering cluster-level logging architectures, pod logs, and container log streams including the PodLogsQuerySplitStreams feature.

manage-resources-containers.md.title: Resource Management for Pods and Containers
manage-resources-containers.md.summary: This guide explains how Kubernetes manages CPU and memory resources within pods and containers, detailing how requests and limits are enforced by the kubelet and kernel, and how memory limits trigger OOM kills.

management.md.title: Managing Workloads
management.md.summary: This page explains how to manage Kubernetes workloads including deploying and scaling services and deployments, organizing resources in YAML files, and using external tools like Helm and Kustomize.

managing-secret-using-config-file.md.title: Managing Secrets using Configuration File
managing-secret-using-config-file.md.summary: This guide explains how to create Kubernetes Secrets using JSON or YAML, including base64 encoding for data, using `stringData` for unencoded values, and deploying them via kubectl.

managing-secret-using-kubectl.md.title: Managing Secrets using kubectl
managing-secret-using-kubectl.md.summary: This page explains how to create, edit, manage, and delete Kubernetes Secrets using the kubectl command-line tool, including methods like raw data and source files.

managing-secret-using-kustomize.md.title: Managing Secrets using Kustomize
managing-secret-using-kustomize.md.summary: This guide explains how to use Kustomize to generate Kubernetes Secrets and ConfigMaps by defining a `secretGenerator` in a `kustomization.yaml` file, storing credentials in text files, and applying the directory to create secure secrets.

managing-tls-in-a-cluster.md.title: Manage TLS Certificates in a Cluster
managing-tls-in-a-cluster.md.summary: This guide explains how to provision TLS certificates signed by a controlled CA using the Kubernetes `certificates.k8s.io` API, including prerequisites like `cfssl`, configuration for custom CA certificates, and steps to request a certificate for a Kubernetes service.

manifest-admission-control.md.title: Manifest-Based Admission Control
manifest-admission-control.md.summary: This page explains how to load admission policies and webhooks from static disk files instead of the Kubernetes API, addressing limitations like bootstrap gaps and etcd dependency.

manifest.md.title: Manifest
manifest.md.summary: A Kubernetes API object in JSON or YAML format that specifies the desired state of an object to be maintained by Kubernetes when applied.

manual-rotation-of-ca-certificates.md.title: Manual Rotation of CA Certificates
manual-rotation-of-ca-certificates.md.summary: This page explains how to manually rotate CA certificates in Kubernetes, including backup procedures, handling bundle conflicts, and restarting kube controllers to update service account secrets with both old and new certificates.

master.md.title: Kubernetes Master Node
master.md.summary: This page explains the role of the Master node in Kubernetes, where it hosts the control plane pods and manages the cluster configuration.

member.md.title: K8s Community Member
member.md.summary: A continuously active contributor in the K8s community who can have issues and PRs assigned to them and participate in special interest groups through GitHub teams.

memory-constraint-namespace.md.title: Configure Minimum and Maximum Memory Constraints for a Namespace
memory-constraint-namespace.md.summary: This page explains how to set minimum and maximum memory limits for containers within a Kubernetes namespace using LimitRange objects. It details the process of creating a namespace, defining a LimitRange with default values, and configuring a Pod to meet these constraints.

memory-default-namespace.md.title: Configure Default Memory Requests and Limits for a Namespace
memory-default-namespace.md.summary: This guide explains how to set default memory limits and requests for Kubernetes namespaces, including how to create a LimitRange and a Pod with containers that inherit these defaults.

memory-manager.md.title: Control Memory Management Policies on a Node
memory-manager.md.summary: This page explains how the Kubernetes Memory Manager ensures guaranteed memory allocation for pods by generating NUMA affinity hints, enforcing cgroups, and managing reserved memory flags. It details prerequisites for CPU and Topology Manager policies, supports Windows via the WindowsCPUAndMemoryAffinity feature, and describes the complete pod admission and deployment flow.

migrate-from-psp.md.title: Migrate from PodSecurityPolicy to the Built-In PodSecurity Admission Controller
migrate-from-psp.md.summary: This page guides users on migrating Kubernetes workloads from PodSecurityPolicies to the built-in PodSecurity Admission Controller, offering a step-by-step approach to minimize risks and security gaps.

migrating-from-dockershim.md.title: Migrating from dockershim
migrating-from-dockershim.md.summary: This guide explains how to migrate from the deprecated Docker Engine runtime (dockershim) to modern container runtimes in Kubernetes, covering prerequisites, migration tasks, and troubleshooting steps.

migrating-telemetry-and-security-agents..title: Migrating Telemetry and Security Agents from Dockerhim
migrating-telemetry-and-security-agents..summary: This guide explains how to migrate telemetry and security agents from Dockerhim to generic tools or alternative runtimes, addressing the deprecation of Docker Engine support in Kubernetes.

mirror-pod.md.title: Mirror Pod
mirror-pod.md.summary: A kubelet-managed static pod that allows kubelet to create a Pod on the API server without requiring manual API server creation, enabling the pod to be visible but not controlled from the API server.

mixed-version-proxy.md.title: Mixed Version Proxy
mixed-version-proxy.md.summary: This page explains Kubernetes's beta feature that allows API servers to proxy resource requests to other peer servers, enabling highly available clusters with safe upgrades by ensuring controllers see complete cluster-wide discovery and directing requests to the correct server during upgrades.

monitor-node-health.md.title: Monitor Node Health
monitor-node-health.md.summary: This page describes how to run Node Problem Detector, a daemon for monitoring node health. It details installation methods via DaemonSet, Addon pods, and ConfigMaps, along with kernel log format limitations and cloud provider addon support.

monitoring.md.title: Monitoring in Kubernetes
monitoring.md.summary: This page provides resources for collecting system metrics and traces for Kubernetes system components.

multi-tenancy.md.title: Multi-tenancy
multi-tenancy.md.summary: This page outlines configuration options and best practices for cluster multi-tenancy in Kubernetes, covering use cases like multiple teams and multiple customers, and defining tenants as either teams or customers depending on the context.

multiple-zones.md.title: Running in multiple zones
multiple-zones.md.summary: This page explains how Kubernetes manages and distributes workloads across multiple failure zones (availability zones) within a region, ensuring high availability by replicating control plane components and pods across these zones.

mutating-admission-policy.md.title: Mutating Admission Policy
mutating-admission-policy.md.summary: This page explains Mutating Admission Policies, which are declarative in-process alternatives to mutating admission webhooks. They use CEL to declare resource mutations via apply configurations or JSON patches, allowing administrators to parameterize and scope policies for Kubernetes resources.

mysql-wordpress-persistent-volume.md.title: Deploying WordPress and MySQL with Persistent Volumes
mysql-wordpress-persistent-volume.md.summary: This tutorial guides users on deploying WordPress and MySQL databases using Minikube, utilizing PersistentVolumes and PersistentVolumeClaims to ensure data survives pod restarts and rescheduling. It covers creating PVs and PVCs, utilizing hostPath storage for local development, and notes that production deployments should use Helm charts instead.

name.md.title: Resource Name
name.md.summary: This page defines a client-provided string used to uniquely identify an object within a resource, such as a pod name. It enforces the rule that only one object of a given kind can have a given name at a time, allowing for name reuse after deletion.

names.md.title: Object Names and IDs
names.md.summary: This page explains how Kubernetes identifies and validates object names and IDs, including naming rules for namespaces, API versions, and DNS subdomains, while noting constraints for physical entities.

namespace.md.title: Namespace
namespace.md.summary: Kubernetes uses namespaces to isolate groups of API resources within a cluster, allowing unique resource names within a single namespace while enforcing scoping rules that apply only to namespaced resources like Pods.

namespaces-walkthrough.md.title: Namespaces Walkthrough
namespaces-walkthrough.md.summary: This guide explains how to create and manage Kubernetes namespaces to partition a cluster, allowing teams to isolate pods, services, and deployments for development and production environments.

namespaces.md.title: Namespaces in Kubernetes
namespaces.md.summary: Kubernetes namespaces provide resource isolation within a cluster, allowing unique names for objects like Deployments and Services while preventing namespace nesting. They are essential for separating users' resources, managing resource quotas, and handling cluster-wide objects like Nodes and StorageClasses.

network-plugins.md.title: Network Plugins
network-plugins.md.summary: This page explains how Kubernetes uses CNI plugins to manage container networking, including requirements for loopback interfaces and hostPort support, and details installation and management procedures.

network-policies.md.title: Network Policies
network-policies.md.summary: This page explains Kubernetes NetworkPolicies, which allow pods to control traffic flow at the IP/port level for TCP, UDP, and SCTP protocols. It details how pods can be isolated for egress or ingress based on specific selectors and IP blocks, and notes that NetworkPolicies are implemented by the network plugin.

network-policy.md.title: Network Policy
network-policy.md.summary: This page explains how pods communicate with each other and network endpoints, how policies enforce port numbers, and how network policies are implemented by supported network plugins.

networking.md.title: Cluster Networking
networking.md.summary: This guide explains Kubernetes networking architecture, covering how Pods, Services, and Nodes interact via IP families (IPv4/IPv6) and dynamic port allocation to prevent port conflicts across a cluster.

node-autoscaling.md.title: Node Autoscaling
node-autoscaling.md.summary: Node autoscaling dynamically provisions or consolidates nodes in a Kubernetes cluster to accommodate workloads, balancing cost and capacity while ensuring pods can be scheduled on available nodes.

node-conformance.md.title: Validate node setup
node-conformance.md.summary: This page explains how to run Kubernetes node conformance tests, including prerequisites like CRI-compatible runtimes and kubelet, and provides shell commands to execute tests on Docker containers.

node-declared-features.md.title: Node Declared Features
node-declared-features.md.summary: Kubernetes nodes report new features via .status.declaredFeatures to ensure Pods only run on nodes that explicitly support them, preventing version skew and improving cluster stability during upgrades.

node-labels.md.title: Node Labels Populated By The Kubelet
node-labels.md.summary: This page explains how Kubernetes nodes are pre-populated with standard labels and how users can override them via kubelet configuration or the Kubernetes API.

node-node.md.title: Kubernetes Node Reference Information
node-node.md.summary: This page provides detailed technical documentation for Kubernetes nodes, covering system components like kubelets, pods, and daemon sets, along with configuration details such as device management, labels, and swap behaviors.

node-overprovisioning.md.title: Overprovisioning Node Capacity for Kubernetes Clusters
node-overprovisioning.md.summary: This page explains how to configure Node overprovisioning in Kubernetes, which proactively reserves compute resources to preempt pods during scaling events and ensure immediate availability during traffic spikes.

node-pod-level-resource-managers.md.title: Pod-level resource managers reference
node-pod-level-resource-managers.md.summary: This document details how Kubernetes kubelet implements Pod-level resource managers, explaining the PodResources gRPC API that tracks CPU and memory allocations at the pod level. It clarifies how exclusive containers report their specific allocations while shared pool containers avoid double-counting by referencing the pod-level allocation instead.

node-pressure-eviction.md.title: Node-pressure Eviction
node-pressure-eviction.md.summary: The kubelet monitors node resources (memory, disk, inodes) and proactively evicts pods when they reach starvation thresholds, setting pods to 'Failed' state to reclaim resources. This differs from API-initiated eviction and respects soft/hard thresholds, with self-healing mechanisms replacing failed pods if managed by a workload object.

node-seccomp.md.title: Seccomp and Kubernetes
node-seccomp.md.summary: This page explains Seccomp, a Linux kernel security feature that restricts process privileges, and how Kubernetes automatically applies these profiles to Pods and containers.

node-shutdown.md.title: Node Shutdowns
node-shutdown.md.summary: This page explains Kubernetes node shutdowns, distinguishing between graceful and non-graceful modes, and details the `unattended-upgrades` package conflict that causes kubelet to fail when shutdown grace period exceeds 30 seconds.

node-status.md.title: Node Status
node-status.md.summary: This page explains how to monitor and maintain Kubernetes node status using `kubectl describe node`, detailing fields like HostName, Conditions (Ready, DiskPressure, etc.), and how to view detailed node information.

node.md.title: Kubernetes Worker Nodes
node.md.summary: This page explains what a node is in Kubernetes, its role as a worker machine that hosts Pods, and the specific services (kubelet, kube-proxy, CRI) it manages.

nodelocaldns.md.title: Using NodeLocal DNSCache in Kubernetes Clusters
nodelocaldns.md.summary: This page explains how NodeLocal DNSCache improves Kubernetes cluster performance by running a DNS caching agent on cluster nodes as a DaemonSet, avoiding DNAT and connection tracking issues while upgrading DNS queries from UDP to TCP.

nodes.md.title: Kubernetes Nodes
nodes.md.summary: This page explains how Kubernetes manages nodes, including their types (virtual/physical), management methods (kubelet registration vs. manual objects), and the health checks required for pods to run on them.

ns-level-pss.md.title: Apply Pod Security Standards at the Namespace Level
ns-level-pss.md.summary: This tutorial guides users on how to enforce the `baseline` Pod Security Standard across a single namespace using Kubernetes labels, following the v1.25 release.

object-management.md.title: Kubernetes Object Management
object-management.md.summary: This guide explains how to manage Kubernetes objects using three distinct techniques: imperative commands (live objects), imperative object configuration (YAML/JSON files), and declarative object configuration (directories). It warns against mixing techniques and details the trade-offs between command-based and file-based management.

object.md.title: Object in Kubernetes
object.md.summary: An API resource representing the desired state of a cluster, managed by the control plane to ensure it exists.

observability.md.title: Kubernetes Observability
observability.md.summary: This page explains how Kubernetes collects, analyzes, and visualizes metrics, logs, and traces to monitor cluster health and performance. It details the three pillars of observability, describes the Prometheus-based metrics pipeline, and covers the Kubernetes Metrics API for resource monitoring.

operator-pattern.md.title: Operator Pattern
operator-pattern.md.summary: This page explains the Operator pattern, a Kubernetes design where a controller links to custom resources. It details how running applications can act as controllers to perform tasks against defined resources in the control plane.

operator.md.title: Operator Pattern
operator.md.summary: This page explains how operators are software extensions to Kubernetes that automate tasks beyond Kubernetes' built-in features, such as deploying, managing backups, and handling upgrades, by linking controllers to custom resources.

optional-kubectl-configs-bash-linux.md.title: bash auto-completion on Linux
optional-kubectl-configs-bash-linux.md.summary: This page explains how to enable kubectl autocompletion on Linux by installing bash-completion and sourcing the completion script into your shell configuration.

optional-kubectl-configs-bash-mac.md.title: bash auto-completion on macOS
optional-kubectl-configs-bash-mac.md.summary: This guide explains how to enable bash auto-completion for kubectl on macOS, requiring Bash 4.1+ and bash-completion v2, with detailed installation steps via Homebrew.

optional-kubectl-configs-fish.md.title: kubectl completion script for Fish
optional-kubectl-configs-fish.md.summary: This page explains how to generate and source the kubectl completion script for Fish, enabling shell autocompletion for kubectl commands.

optional-kubectl-configs-pwsh.md.title: PowerShell auto-completion
optional-kubectl-configs-pwsh.md.summary: This guide explains how to generate and integrate kubectl completion scripts into PowerShell profiles to enable auto-completion for shell sessions.

optional-kubectl-configs-zsh.md.title: kubectl completion script for Zsh
optional-kubectl-configs-zsh.md.summary: This guide explains how to generate and source the kubectl completion script for Zsh, enabling autocompletion across all shell sessions.

organize-cluster-access-kubeconfig.md.title: Organizing Cluster Access Using kubeconfig Files
organize-cluster-access-kubeconfig.md.summary: This guide explains how to use kubeconfig files to organize cluster, user, and namespace information for secure cluster access. It details how to define contexts, merge multiple files, and safely manage kubeconfig files from trusted sources.

overview.md.title: Overview of Kubernetes
overview.md.summary: Kubernetes is a container orchestration platform that manages distributed applications by handling scaling, failover, and self-healing. It provides services like load balancing, storage orchestration, and automated rollouts to ensure production environments remain resilient and stable.

owners-dependents.md.title: Owners and Dependents
owners-dependents.md.summary: This page explains Kubernetes dependency relationships where objects like ReplicaSets are owners of Pods and DaemonSets. It details how dependent objects use metadata fields like ownerReferences and blockOwnerDeletion to manage garbage collection, cross-namespace rules, and controller permissions.

parallel-processing-expansion.md.title: Parallel Processing using Expansions
parallel-processing-expansion.md.summary: This guide demonstrates how to run multiple jobs in parallel using a common template, specifically using the 'expand' feature of Kubernetes Jobs. It shows how to download a YAML template, replace placeholders like $ITEM with loop variables, and create multiple Job manifests that can be executed concurrently.

persistent-volume-claim.md.title: Persistent Volume Claim
persistent-volume-claim.md.summary: This page explains how to claim storage resources from a PersistentVolume, detailing how to specify storage size, access mode (read-only, read-write, exclusive), and reclaim behavior (retained, recycled, or deleted).

persistent-volume.md.title: Persistent Volume
persistent-volume.md.summary: This page explains Persistent Volume (PV) as an API object representing pluggable storage resources that persist beyond Pod lifecycles, enabling static provisioning. It contrasts PVs with PersistentVolumeClaims (PVCs) for dynamic provisioning scenarios.

persistent-volumes.md.title: Persistent Volumes
persistent-volumes.md.summary: This document describes Kubernetes Persistent Volumes (PVs) and Persistent Volume Claims (PVCs), explaining how administrators provision storage for pods and how to manage varying volume properties like performance and access modes.

pid-limiting.md.title: Process ID Limits And Reservations
pid-limiting.md.summary: Kubernetes limits Pod process IDs (PIDs) to prevent PID exhaustion that crashes host daemons like kubelet, and reserves system PIDs for node overhead. Administrators can configure these limits via kubelet command-line options to protect pods and prevent cluster-wide crashes.

platform-developer.md.title: Platform Developer
platform-developer.md.summary: A role where developers customize Kubernetes to fit project needs, utilizing custom resources or API extensions to add application-specific functionality.

pod-condition.md.title: Pod Conditions
pod-condition.md.summary: Kubernetes documentation explaining how Pod Conditions track the state of pods across phases like Scheduled, Ready, and ReadyToStartContainers, complementing the lifecycle phase to provide detailed health metrics for troubleshooting.

pod-disruption-budget.md.title: Pod Disruption Budget
pod-disruption-budget.md.summary: A PDB limits the number of pods that can be evicted involuntarily, ensuring a certain percentage of pods remain available while constraining the total workload.

pod-disruption.md.title: Pod Disruption
pod-disruption.md.summary: This page explains how Pods on Nodes are terminated, covering both intentional (voluntary) and unintentional (involuntary) scenarios.

pod-failure-policy.md.title: Handling retriable and non-retriable pod failures with Pod failure policy
pod-failure-policy.md.summary: This document explains how to configure a Pod failure policy to avoid unnecessary pod retries by detecting non-retriable failures (e.g., software bugs) and ignoring disruptions like preemption or taint-based eviction.

pod-hostname.md.title: Pod Hostname
pod-hostname.md.summary: This page explains how to set a Pod's hostname, potential side effects after configuration, and the underlying mechanics, including how hostname and FQDN are derived from metadata.name and optional subdomain fields.

pod-level-resource-managers.md.title: Pod-level resource managers
pod-level-resource-managers.md.summary: This page explains how pod-level resource managers extend traditional resource managers (CPU, Memory) to handle per-pod resource specifications. It details how these managers partition resources into exclusive slices for containers requesting them and shared pools for others, enabling hybrid allocation models suitable for performance-sensitive workloads.

pod-lifecycle.md.title: Pod Lifecycle
pod-lifecycle.md.summary: This page describes the complete lifecycle of a Pod, including phases like Pending, Running, Succeeded, and Failed, explaining how the kubelet manages containers, handles faults, and manages scheduling and garbage collection.

pod-overhead.md.title: Pod Overhead in Kubernetes
pod-overhead.md.summary: Kubernetes manages Pod overhead by accounting for system resources consumed by the Pod infrastructure (cgroups, memory, CPU) on top of container requests and limits. This overhead is calculated at admission time and applied to resource calculations for scheduling, cgroup sizing, and eviction ranking.

pod-priority-preemption.md.title: Pod Priority and Preemption
pod-priority-preemption.md.summary: This page explains how pods can have priority to prevent scheduling conflicts, how administrators can set PriorityClasses to control pod creation, and the system's built-in critical PriorityClasses for system components.

pod-priority.md.title: Pod Priority
pod-priority.md.summary: Pod Priority defines the importance of a pod relative to others, allowing administrators to set scheduling priority to be higher or lower for production clusters.

pod-qos.md.title: Pod Quality of Service Classes
pod-qos.md.summary: Kubernetes classifies Pods into Guaranteed, Burstable, and BestEffort classes based on resource requests and limits. Guaranteed pods have strict limits and are least likely to be evicted, while BestEffort pods are evicted first when Node pressure occurs. This classification helps Kubernetes decide which Pods to evict from a Node to manage resource constraints.

pod-scheduling-readiness.md.title: Pod Scheduling Readiness
pod-scheduling-readiness.md.summary: This documentation explains Kubernetes Pod scheduling readiness, detailing how pods are marked as ready or gated for scheduling via the `schedulingGates` field. It covers configuration, usage examples, and observability metrics like `scheduler_pending_pods` to manage pods that may remain in a 'miss-essential-resources' state.

pod-security-admission.md.title: Pod Security Admission
pod-security-admission.md.summary: Kubernetes's built-in admission controller enforces Pod Security Standards (privileged, baseline, restricted) at namespace creation. Users configure namespace-level labels to enforce, audit, or warn against violations, allowing different levels per mode.

pod-security-policy.md.title: Pod Security Policies
pod-security-policy.md.summary: Kubernetes v1.21 removed Pod Security Policies (PSP), allowing migration to Pod Security Admission (PSA) or third-party plugins. This guide details how to enforce similar security restrictions using PSA or custom plugins.

pod-security-standards.md.title: Pod Security Standards
pod-security-standards.md.summary: This guide outlines three cumulative policies (Privileged, Baseline, and Restricted) designed to cover the security spectrum, ensuring that privileged workloads like Windows Pods cannot bypass isolation mechanisms while enforcing hardening best practices.

pod-sidecar-containers.md.title: Adopting Sidecar Containers
pod-sidecar-containers.md.summary: This guide explains how Kubernetes allows running sidecar containers alongside regular application containers within a Pod, offering benefits like graceful termination and avoiding restart policy conflicts.

pod-template.md.title: PodTemplate API
pod-template.md.summary: This API defines common metadata like labels and template names for Pods, along with specifying desired pod states. It is embedded in workload management APIs such as Deployment and StatefulSets to manage Pods.

pod.md.title: Pod
pod.md.summary: A Kubernetes object representing a set of running containers on a cluster, typically managed by a deployment.

podgroup-api-lifecycle.md.title: PodGroup Lifecycle
podgroup-api-lifecycle.md.summary: This page explains how PodGroups are created, protected, and managed by workloads. It details their lifecycle, ownership rules, creation ordering, deletion protection, and specific limitations regarding Pod scheduling constraints.

podgroup-api.md.title: PodGroup API
podgroup-api.md.summary: The PodGroup API defines a runtime scheduling unit for Pods, carrying scheduling policies and status. It supports Gang and Basic policies, priority classes, and resource claims for DRA devices, enabling complex workload scheduling.

podgroup-scheduling.md.title: PodGroup Scheduling
podgroup-scheduling.md.summary: This page explains Kubernetes PodGroup scheduling, where a group of Pods is evaluated as a single unit to prevent resource deadlocks. The scheduler uses a snapshot-based cycle to find valid node placements for the entire group simultaneously, ensuring all Pods are bound if sufficient resources are available.

podgroup.md.title: PodGroup
podgroup.md.summary: A PodGroup is a runtime object representing a group of Pods scheduled together as a single unit, carrying both scheduling policies and status.

pods-and-endpoint-termination-flow.md.title: Explore Termination Behavior for Pods And Their Endpoints
pods-and-endpoint-termination-flow.md.summary: This tutorial demonstrates the graceful connection draining process for Kubernetes Pods and their associated endpoints, using an nginx web server to illustrate the termination flow and endpoint state changes.

pods-some-nodes.md.title: Running Pods on Only Some Nodes
pods-some-nodes.md.summary: This page explains how to configure a DaemonSet to run only pods on nodes with specific labels (e.g., `ssd=true`) to optimize performance by leveraging local SSD storage.

pods.md.title: Pods in Kubernetes
pods.md.summary: Pods are the smallest deployable units in Kubernetes, allowing applications to run as tightly coupled containers within shared namespaces and filesystems. They model logical hosts where applications are co-located and tightly coupled, enabling efficient resource management and scaling.

policies.md.title: PodGroup Scheduling Policies
policies.md.summary: This documentation explains how PodGroup scheduling policies are defined in Kubernetes Workload APIs, detailing the `basic` and `gang` policy types, their use cases for observability vs. tight coupling, and how they are applied via PodGroupTemplates or directly on standalone PodGroups.

policy.md.title: Kubernetes Policies
policy.md.summary: This page explains Kubernetes policies, which are configurations managing runtime behaviors. It details how policies can be applied via API objects, admission controllers, and dynamic admission control, including examples like image pull policies and validating admission policies.

port-forward-access-application-cluster..title: kubectl port-forward MongoDB in Kubernetes
port-forward-access-application-cluster..summary: This guide explains how to use `kubectl port-forward` to connect to a MongoDB server running in a Kubernetes cluster, enabling debugging and testing of database connections.

ports-and-protocols.md.title: Ports and Protocols
ports-and-protocols.md.summary: This page details Kubernetes control plane and worker node protocols, including TCP and UDP port ranges for API servers, etcd, kube-apiserver, kube-scheduler, and kube-controller-manager, along with default and custom port configurations for NodePort Services.

preemption.md.title: Preemption Logic in Kubernetes
preemption.md.summary: Kubernetes uses preemption to allow a pending pod to find a suitable node by evicting low-priority pods on that node. If a pod cannot be scheduled, the scheduler attempts to preempt lower-priority pods to enable scheduling for the pending one.

priority-class.md.title: PriorityClass
priority-class.md.summary: A named class for scheduling priority assigned to a Pod, mapping a name to an integer value (range -2147483648 to 1000000000) used for preemption.

probe.md.title: Probe
probe.md.summary: A check performed by kubelet against a running container to define its state and health, informing its lifecycle.

probes.md.title: Liveness, Readiness, and Startup Probes

proxies.md.title: Proxies in Kubernetes

replicationcontroller.md.title: ReplicationController
replicationcontroller.md.summary: ReplicationController ensures a specified number of pod replicas run simultaneously, automatically replacing failed pods and serving as a process supervisor for Kubernetes workloads.

scheduling-framework.md.summary: This page describes a pluggable Kubernetes scheduler architecture where plugins compile directly into the scheduler. secret.md.title: Kubernetes Secrets

secrets-good-practices.md.title: Good practices for Kubernetes Secrets
secrets-good-practices.md.summary: This page outlines security and management guidelines for Kubernetes Secrets, including encryption at rest, least-privilege access control, and proper etcd management policies.

securing-a-cluster.md.title: Securing a Cluster
securing-a-cluster.md.summary: This document outlines the security measures for protecting a Kubernetes cluster, emphasizing the use of TLS for API traffic, authentication mechanisms, and RBAC to prevent accidental or malicious access.

security-checklist.md.summary: This document outlines a comprehensive security checklist for Kubernetes environments, covering authentication, authorization, network security, and best practices. security-context.md.title: Configure a Security Context for a Pod or Container

sidecar-containers.md.summary: Sidecar containers are secondary containers within a Pod that run alongside the main application container, providing services like logging or monitoring without modifying the application code. sig.md.title: SIG (Special Interest Group) in Kubernetes

switch-to-evented-pleg.md.summary: This page details how to migrate nodes to use event-based updates for container status, reducing resource consumption by the kubelet compared to legacy polling. It details how the manager acts as a source of truth for hint providers, rejecting hints that cause latency and accepting only those that align with the configured narrowest preferred mask.

topology-spread-constraints.md.title: Pod Topology Spread Constraints
topology-spread-constraints.md.summary: This documentation explains how to configure cluster-level topology spread constraints using the `topologySpreadConstraints` field in Pod YAML, allowing you to enforce high availability and efficient resource utilization by limiting pod distribution across regions, nodes, and other domains.

topology.md.title: Troubleshooting Topology Management
topology.md.summary: This guide explains how Kubernetes topology management errors like TopologyAffinityError occur and how to diagnose them using pod status, system logs, and kubelet state files.

translate-compose-kubernetes.md.title: Translate a Docker Compose File to Kubernetes Resources
translate-compose-kubernetes.md.summary: This guide explains how to convert a Docker Compose configuration file into Kubernetes resources using Kompose, including installation methods and the step-by-step process of converting a YAML file to YAML service files and deployments.

troubleshoot-kubectl.md.title: Troubleshooting kubectl
troubleshoot-kubectl.md.summary: This guide explains how to diagnose and resolve kubectl-related issues, covering cluster setup, verifying kubectl installation, checking kubeconfig, VPN connectivity, and authentication errors.

troubleshooting-cni-plugin-related-error.title: Troubleshooting CNI plugin-related errors
troubleshooting-cni-plugin-related-error.summary: This page explains how to resolve CNI plugin-related errors, specifically focusing on 'Incompatible CNI versions' and 'Failed to destroy network for sandbox' errors that occur when containerd v1.6.0-v1.6.3 is used without upgrading CNI plugins or declaring the CNI config version.

troubleshooting-kubeadm.md.title: Troubleshooting kubeadm
troubleshooting-kubeadm.md.summary: This page provides common failure scenarios for kubeadm installation and running, including issues with missing RBAC permissions, missing system executables like ebtables, and control plane readiness issues that may cause kubeadm to hang during installation.

ttlafterfinished.md.title: Automatic Cleanup for Finished Jobs
ttlafterfinished.md.summary: This page explains how Kubernetes' TTL-after-finished controller limits the lifetime of Job objects to prevent orphaned resources. It details how to set this TTL via manifest fields, mutating webhooks, or custom controllers, and warns against modifying TTL after expiration due to Kubernetes's lack of guarantee on retained objects.

tutorials.md.title: Kubernetes Tutorials
tutorials.md.summary: This page lists interactive and instructional tutorials covering Kubernetes basics, configuration, stateful applications, services, security, and cluster management.

uid.md.title: UID
uid.md.summary: A Kubernetes system-generated string that uniquely identifies objects across the entire cluster lifespan, designed to distinguish between historical occurrences of similar entities.

update-api-object-kubectl-patch.md.title: kubectl patch for strategic merge and JSON merge patches
update-api-object-kubectl-patch.md.summary: This guide demonstrates how to use kubectl patch to update API objects in place, specifically showing a strategic merge patch that adds a new container to an existing one without replacing it.

update-daemon-set.md.title: Perform a Rolling Update on a DaemonSet
update-daemon-set.md.summary: This page explains how to perform a rolling update on a DaemonSet, detailing the OnDelete and RollingUpdate update strategies, and provides Kubectl commands to create, verify, and update DaemonSets with the RollingUpdate strategy.

update-deployment-rolling.md.title: Update a Deployment Without Downtime
update-deployment-rolling.md.summary: This page explains how to safely update a running Kubernetes Deployment using a rolling update, gradually replacing old Pods with new ones while maintaining application availability.

update-intro.md.title: Performing a Rolling Update
update-intro.md.summary: This guide explains how to use kubectl to perform rolling updates for Deployments, ensuring zero downtime by incrementally replacing Pods with new ones while maintaining service availability.

updating-configuration-via-a-configmap.m.title: Updating Configuration via a ConfigMap
updating-configuration-via-a-configmap.m.summary: This page provides step-by-step examples of updating application configuration within a Pod using a ConfigMap, including creating a ConfigMap from literal values and mounting it as a volume to load environment variables and data into a running container.

upgrading-linux-nodes.md.title: Upgrading Linux nodes
upgrading-linux-nodes.md.summary: This page guides users on upgrading Linux Worker Nodes created with kubeadm, including updating package repositories, upgrading kubeadm and kubectl, and draining the node to prepare for maintenance.

upgrading-windows-nodes.md.title: Upgrading Windows nodes
upgrading-windows-nodes.md.summary: This page guides users on how to upgrade Windows nodes created with kubeadm, including draining the node, syncing kubelet configuration, and restarting kubelet and kube-proxy.

upstream.md.title: Upstream (disambiguation)
upstream.md.summary: This page explains the technical convention of using 'upstream' to refer to the core Kubernetes codebase or a forked repository, contrasting it with 'downstream' for the forked version.

use-cascading-deletion.md.title: Use Cascading Deletion in a Cluster
use-cascading-deletion.md.summary: This page explains how to configure cascading deletion types (foreground and background) for garbage collection in Kubernetes clusters, including deployment creation, pod owner reference checks, and kubectl API commands.

use-pod-level-resource-managers.md.title: Use Pod-Level Resources with kubelet Resource Managers
use-pod-level-resource-managers.md.summary: This tutorial explains how to configure kubelet resource managers (CPU, memory, topology) to support pod-level resource specifications, enabling hybrid allocation models where exclusive containers receive NUMA-aligned resources while others share a pod-level shared pool.

user-guide.md.title: Guide for Running Windows Containers in Kubernetes
user-guide.md.summary: This page provides a walkthrough for running Windows containers using Kubernetes, highlighting Windows-specific functionality within Kubernetes and noting that deployment steps are identical to Linux. It details how to create a manifest for a Windows web server deployment on a Windows node.

user-impersonation.md.title: User Impersonation
user-impersonation.md.summary: User impersonation allows authenticated users to act as another user, group, or service account via HTTP headers, enabling API requests to bypass authentication checks for the impersonated entity.

user-namespaces.md.title: User Namespaces in Kubernetes
user-namespaces.md.summary: User namespaces allow pods to isolate user running inside containers from host users, granting full privileges within the namespace but unprivileged outside. This mitigates security risks by preventing compromised containers from damaging host resources or other pods.

userns.md.title: User Namespace
userns.md.summary: A Linux kernel feature allowing non-root users to emulate root privileges for container isolation, mitigating container break-out attacks.

validate-dual-stack.md.title: Validate IPv4/IPv6 dual-stack
validate-dual-stack.md.summary: This guide explains how to validate Kubernetes clusters supporting dual-stack networking, ensuring nodes have single IPv4 and IPv6 address blocks, and verifying Pod IPs via the Downward API.

validating-admission-policy.md.title: Validating Admission Policy
validating-admission-policy.md.summary: This page explains how Validating Admission Policies work using Common Expression Language (CEL) to declaratively validate admission rules. It details the three required resources (Policy, Parameter, Binding) and provides a guide for creating policies with bindings, including a sample YAML configuration.

verify-kubectl.md.title: Verify Kubectl Install
verify-kubectl.md.summary: This page explains how to check and troubleshoot the configuration of kubectl to access a Kubernetes cluster, including checking cluster state via kubectl cluster-info and resolving errors like 'No Auth Provider Found' by installing Minikube or using specific plugins.

verify-signed-artifacts.md.title: Verify Signed Kubernetes Artifacts
verify-signed-artifacts.md.summary: This guide explains how to verify binary signatures (e.g., kubectl) and image signatures (e.g., kube-apiserver) using cosign, including keyless signing methods and specific verification commands for stable releases.

vertical-pod-autoscale.md.title: Vertical Pod Autoscaling
vertical-pod-autoscale.md.summary: Kubernetes's VPA automatically adjusts resource requests and limits for workloads (like Deployments) to match actual usage, preventing waste when demand exceeds optimal levels.

virtual-ips.md.title: Virtual IPs and Service Proxies
virtual-ips.md.summary: This page explains how Kubernetes uses kube-proxy to forward inbound traffic to backend services, addressing issues with DNS TTLs and caching. It details kube-proxy's role in managing Service and EndpointSlice state, noting that kernel-level rules may persist after reboot and that cleanup is optional.

volume-attributes-classes.md.title: Volume Attributes Classes
volume-attributes-classes.md.summary: This page explains how administrators define mutable storage class qualities using VolumeAttributesClasses in Kubernetes, allowing dynamic provisioning and modification of PersistentVolumes based on driver-specific parameters like IOPS and throughput.

volume-health-monitoring.md.title: CSI Volume Health Monitoring
volume-health-monitoring.md.summary: CSI volume health monitoring allows CSI drivers to report health problems directly to Kubernetes via CSI RPCs, enabling automated monitoring of PersistentVolumeClaims, Pods, and Storage Nodes.

volume-plugin.md.title: Volume Plugin
volume-plugin.md.summary: A Volume Plugin enables Pod storage integration by allowing users to attach and mount storage volumes independently of Kubernetes code, offering both tree and out-of-tree deployment options.

volume-populators-and-data-sources.md.title: Volume Populators and Data Sources
volume-populators-and-data-sources.md.summary: This document explains Kubernetes volume populators and data sources, detailing how they work with PersistentVolumeClaims and how custom volume populators extend the built-in clone/restore mechanisms.

volume-pvc-datasource.md.title: CSI Volume Cloning
volume-pvc-datasource.md.summary: This document explains how to clone existing Kubernetes PersistentVolumeClaims (PVCs) using CSI VolumePVCDataSource, ensuring the cloned volume is a direct copy of the source with the same namespace and storage class.

volume-snapshot-classes.md.title: Volume Snapshot Classes
volume-snapshot-classes.md.summary: This document defines VolumeSnapshotClass in Kubernetes, a resource that allows administrators to define storage classes for dynamically provisioning volume snapshots. It details required fields like driver, deletion policy, and parameters, explains how default classes are selected based on PVC StorageClass drivers, and notes that multiple default classes must not coexist for the same CSI driver.

volume-snapshots.md.title: Volume Snapshots
volume-snapshots.md.summary: This page explains Kubernetes Volume Snapshots, which are CRDs allowing administrators to create volume snapshots for backup or recreation. It details the required CSI drivers, snapshot controller, and sidecar helper, and notes that these features are not available by default on all clusters.

volume.md.title: Volume
volume.md.summary: A Kubernetes volume is a persistent storage resource that persists across pod restarts, allowing data to survive container lifecycle changes. It is accessible to containers within a pod and is managed by the Kubernetes cluster.

volumes.md.title: Kubernetes Volumes
volumes.md.summary: Kubernetes volumes enable containers to share data and persist state across pod restarts by providing filesystem access via PersistentVolumes, EphemeralVolumes, and other types.

watch.md.title: Watch
watch.md.summary: Watch is a Kubernetes verb used to track changes to objects as a stream, enabling efficient detection of changes like ConfigMap updates without polling.

web-ui-dashboard.md.title: Kubernetes Dashboard - Deprecation and Access Guide
web-ui-dashboard.md.summary: This page explains that the Kubernetes Dashboard is deprecated and unmaintained, directing users to Headlamp for new installations. It details the deployment method using Helm, the RBAC configuration requiring a Bearer Token, and provides a Kubectl port-forward command to access the dashboard at localhost:8443.

webhook.md.title: Webhook Mode
webhook.md.summary: This page explains how Kubernetes uses HTTP POST to trigger Webhook events, specifically for user privilege queries. It details the configuration format for the authorization webhook config file, including cluster and API server settings, and describes the JSON payload required for SubjectAccessReview requests.

wg.md.title: WG (working group)
wg.md.summary: A working group facilitates the discussion and implementation of short-lived, narrow, or decoupled projects for committees, SIGs, or cross-SIG efforts.

what-happens-on-restart.md.title: Node Restart Behavior
what-happens-on-restart.md.summary: This page details the effects of a node restart, specifically focusing on kubelet and container restarts. It explains that running containers continue to run during a restart, while the node becomes 'NotReady' until the kubelet finishes initializing. It notes that resetting container readiness on every restart places a significant load on the API server and could temporarily remove healthy Pods from load balancing, though a feature gate allows reverting to the default behavior.

windows-networking.md.title: Networking on Windows
windows-networking.md.summary: This page explains Kubernetes node networking on Windows, detailing how CNI plugins manage virtual networks, namespaces, and policies while distinguishing host registry-based configuration from container-specific APIs.

windows-resource-management.md.title: Resource Management for Windows nodes
windows-resource-management.md.summary: This page details how Linux and Windows differ in resource management, noting that Windows lacks an OOM killer and uses a Job object per container with system namespace filtering to prevent privileged containers from running on the host.

windows-security.md.title: Security For Windows Nodes
windows-security.md.summary: This page outlines critical security considerations for Windows nodes, including using file ACLs and BitLocker for secret data protection, configuring container users (ContainerUser vs. ContainerAdministrator), and implementing pod-level isolation to avoid unsupported privileged container security contexts.

windows-storage.md.title: Windows Storage
windows-storage.md.summary: This page explains Windows' layered filesystem driver using NTFS, container layering, and volume mounting limitations. It details unsupported features like volume subpath mounts, host projection, and read-only filesystems, while noting that Kubernetes volumes (FlexVolume and CSI) are the primary tools for managing persistent storage on Windows nodes.

windows.md.title: Windows in Kubernetes
windows.md.summary: This page explains how Kubernetes supports worker nodes running either Linux or Windows, emphasizing a vendor-neutral approach for joining Windows servers as nodes. It details various configuration steps for managing Windows nodes, including networking, storage, resource management, and security, alongside guides for scheduling and debugging.

working-with-objects.md.title: Objects In Kubernetes
working-with-objects.md.summary: This page explains how Kubernetes objects are represented in the API and how to express them in YAML, covering concepts like spec and status.

workload-api-topology-aware-scheduling.m.title: Topology-Aware Workload Scheduling
workload-api-topology-aware-scheduling.m.summary: TAS optimizes pod placement by forcing all pods in a PodGroup into a single topology domain (e.g., rack or zone) to minimize latency and prevent fragmentation. It uses gang scheduling to ensure at least minCount pods fit together before committing resources, preventing preemption and ensuring new pods land on the same domain even if some are already scheduled.

workload-api.md.title: Workload API
workload-api.md.summary: This page explains the Workload API resource in Kubernetes, which defines static scheduling policies for multi-Pod applications. It details how PodGroupTemplates are used to create PodGroups, specifies immutable spec fields, and notes that priority and disruption modes are feature-gated.

workload-aware-preemption.md.title: Workload-Aware Preemption
workload-aware-preemption.md.summary: This documentation explains the workload-aware preemption mechanism in Kubernetes, where a PodGroup is treated as a single preemptor unit to maximize cluster scheduling space. It details how the scheduler evaluates cluster-wide victims based on a strict priority hierarchy (priority, workload type, group size, and start time) to determine which pods to preempt and how to handle other PodGroups.

workload.md.title: Workload
workload.md.summary: This page defines a workload as an application running on Kubernetes and details the core objects like DaemonSet, Deployment, Job, ReplicaSet, and StatefulSet that compose it.

workloadbuilder.md.title: Scheduling Building Block APIs and the workloadbuilder Library
workloadbuilder.md.summary: This documentation explains how reusable scheduling API building blocks are defined and compiled into the workloadbuilder library, allowing controllers to express complex scheduling intents like gang scheduling with a consistent schema across the Kubernetes ecosystem.

workloads.md.title: Workloads
workloads.md.summary: This page explains Kubernetes workloads, including Pods, Deployments, StatefulSets, DaemonSets, Jobs, and CronJobs, detailing how they manage containers and their lifecycle.

zookeeper.md.title: Running ZooKeeper on Kubernetes
zookeeper.md.summary: This tutorial explains how to deploy Apache ZooKeeper using StatefulSets and PodDisruptionBudgets in a Kubernetes cluster, covering prerequisites, deployment configuration, and ensuring service availability during maintenance.
